description: 2048 is a simple but well made text-mode game that is exactly what you probably expect: A version of the popular 2048 mobile puzzle game. The object is to smush numbered blocks of the same value together to progressively increase their value, doubling each time, until you reach the mythical 2048. Here the game is presented in colorful ANSI-like style with intuitive WASD keys for shifting the pieces. You can restart to begin a new game, and your progress is automatically saved when you quit.

title: 3-Demon
description: 3-Demon is probably the strangest Pac-Man game you'll ever play. It is played in a first-person perspective, that is, in "3D". How does this work, you may be asking? Well it's kind of difficult to figure out where you're going, and where the ghosts are. Luckily there's sort of a radar at the bottom that tells you how close the ghosts are. Overall it's poor graphics and dated sounds don't detract much from the game, so it's probably unique enough to be worth checking out. Is this the first "3D shooting" game ever? Not really but it's still interesting!

title: 3D Bomber
description: 3D Bomber is a 3D version of Bomberman. You can play against the computer, or with a human opponent via modem or null modem cable. (Not sure how viable that is nowadays so you may need to be content with the single player game.) The game plays similarly to the classic Bomberman game, except that all the action takes place in a 3D first-person perspective, Wolfenstein 3D type environment. As you might except, it's rather difficult to navigate the maze-like level when you can only see what's directly around you. You can't plan and strategically go after your opponent. The author probably realized this because there is a tiny mini-map added to the bottom corner which is barely visible. In practice, you'll need to try to use this to see where your opponent is. However that means that the 3D element becomes almost superfluous.

title: 3D Xmas Adventure: Santa's Rescue
description: Spread the holiday cheer with this mediocre somewhat-Christmas themed game! It was released by Pie in the Sky Software to promote their 3D game creation system. As such, it's a decent game made with it, but it's still not great. There is a story in the game but it's not too important. You're running around outside in a forest with a lot of trees. A candy cane is your only weapon (?!) and you have to pick up Christmas stockings which work as ammo (?!?!). The original website describes it like this: "Armed with a magic candy cane that shoots jingles and sprinkles, you run around the North Pole gathering gifts, freeing grounded reindeer, and thawing out elves. Beware of the growling abominable snowmen and the menacing grinchy creatures!" Generally it looks and sounds okay, and as with all Pie in the Sky 3D games, it plays a bit too twitchy. It's not obvious what you're supposed to do or where to go, or even which characters are enemies.

title: 4D Boxing
description: 4D Boxing attempts to recreate the sport of boxing more accurately than a lot of popular computer or arcade game based on the sport. It uses a graphics system that was, for the time, quite revolutionary; it was "created with TRU-MOTIONtm, an astonishing new technique that uses filled polygons to replicate human motion!" It's more like rock'em sock'em robot motion, but the game was nonetheless revolutionary for its time, and features decent graphics and sound effects, as well as complex controls which give you a lot of variety when maneuvering your fighter, and other simulation elements like boxer statistics. (Note: Run BOX.BAT to start the game.)

title: 688 Attack Sub
description: 688 Attack Sub is a submarine simulation game, taking place during the cold war era. The player can perform various missions and can choose to control American or Soviet submarines. The focus here is on "realism" rather than action, and you'll need to learn the various different systems of the submarine in order to make progress. This demo version apparently came as some sort of bonus on Maxell diskettes, since there are constant references to Maxell during the game. (It even notes during the tutorial that certain features were omitted in this demo since they wouldn't it on the single floppy disk!) The demo does include a tutorial of sorts, although it doesn't explain how to play, just what the various options within the subsystems do. This is not my kind of game so I didn't invest too much time into trying to figure out what everything does. The graphics are decent for the time and it offers mouse control, and the full version offered multiplayer over modem, which I think was pretty good for the time period. I do remember that during grade school in the early 90's several of my friends were obsessed with this game so if you're into simulation war games give it a try.

title: Absence
description: Absence is a mod (total conversion, I would say) of Wolfenstein 3D. After id Software released the Wolf3D source code, many people made their own maps, mods, and full conversions, of which Absence is recognized as being ground-breaking and worthwhile within the community. It of course include new levels, a new storyline, new graphics and sounds (although many are ripped from other games like DOOM) and the addition of new features not found in Wolf3D, such as finding written notes, or acquiring items from walls. If you enjoy Wolf3D you will likely also enjoy this game. (Note: The yellow keycard in the first level is tough to find but keep searching, you'll find it eventually! It's location is a seeeecret ...)

title: Abuse
description: Abuse is a great side-scrolling action game that uses a unique system to control your character. You use the keyboard to move around and the mouse to aim your gun. It works pretty well and the game can be great fun to play, since it has nicely done graphics and sound effects, as well as many non-linear levels and powerups. (Also check out the fan-made project based on the original source code, fRaBs!) Video ReviewVideo review of Abuse, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Acid Tetris
description: Basically a Tetris game ... but a GREAT looking and sounding one. Very nice graphics and exceptional music. Beyond that, it's just a variant of Tetris that doesn't offer a lot of new features. If you only download one Tetris game, however, this should be it. Very nice indeed. By default, use the left and right arrow keys to move, down to drop, and use the A and S keys to rotate the blocks. (Note that this game is now known as "Super ACiD Block Attack", probably due to legal concerns from using the "Tetris" name.)

title: Action Supercross
description: Action Supercross (it's now called "Elasto Mania" in more recent Windows versions) is a motorbike simulation game that lets you drive your motorbike around a bunch of fun levels, bouncing and crashing into stuff. It features nice graphics, realistic physics, and the ability to create your own new content for the game. In fact many people seem to enjoy creating new levels, graphics etc for this game, as evidenced by the fan sites that are/were popular online. Now there are even two pseudo-sequels for Windows and an iOS app, all using the "Elasto Mania" name. The physics model may or may not be as accurate as claimed; it's definitely not an arcade racer, and you will likely crash often! (Fun fact: This game was referenced in an XKCD comic!)

title: ADOM Ancient Domains of Mystery
description: If you enjoy Roguelike games, you'll want to try ADOM. (Its full name is "Ancient Domains of Mystery".) It features primitive ASCII graphics (like most Roguelikes) but it is very in-depth, even more so than Nethack. The game takes place not only in dungeons, but on the overworld and in towns as well. It is constantly being updated, so you may want to visit the ADOM homepage to check for new versions. There is now a full graphical updated version available on GOG.com.

title: Aethra Chronicles: Volume One - Celystra's Bane
description: The Aethra Chronicles is an in-depth roleplaying game where you build a party of three adventurers (somewhat painstakingly so with all the different options) before venturing out on your epic quest! You can also acquire hired helpers during the game, for a maximum party of six heroes! This RPG was apparently based on the real-world Rolemaster pen-and-paper RPGs, which helps explain its depth. The presentation of the game is good, with detailed graphics and MIDI music, although the music repeats rather frequently. The gameplay is classic PC RPG type stuff, with certain elements borrowed from the SSI "Gold Box" series of games. Definitely not a game to play casually, but if you're looking for an in-depth long-term investment, this might be your game. (Probably download and play offline if that's the case ...)

title: Albion
description: Albion is an innovative sci-fi RPG with some unique features and also a unique interface. Set in the year 2227, a scientist crash lands on a planet thought to be uninhabited, only to discover there is a rich variety of life there. You explore some areas in a traditional overhead 2D mode, while others in a first-person 3D mode. There are plenty of richly detailed environments to explore (this demo contains the first two scenarios from the full game) and plenty of NPCs to encounter and enemies to fight. The interface can be a bit tricky to get used to and many people dislike it. Nonetheless many consider it a forgotten classic in the RPG genre. WARNING: Playing DOSBOX_ALBIONFIX.ZIP on your own PC will likely not work. It is specifically set up for in-browser play. Download albion.zip and install the game locally instead. Video ReviewVideo review of Albion, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Aldo 1: Aldo's Adventure
description: Aldo bears a striking resemblence to Mario in this EGA ladder-climbing and jumping game that looks suspiciously similar to the original Donkey Kong game. Obvious similarities aside, this game does feature excellent play control, and the game holds up very well even though it's now over 15 years old! Like Donkey Kong each level fills one screen and does not scroll, although there are several different levels to explore.

title: Alien Cabal
description: Alien Cabal is a FPS where aliens have invaded, and it's your job (apparently) to kill them. However in my testing I didn't encounter any aliens, just identical guys in suits whose sole purpose in life seemed to be to run up to me and shoot me in the face. As fun as that sounds, unless you enjoy hearing terrible sound effects (be ready to hear "You're not authorized!" shouted at you repeatedly) and strange graphics, you probably won't be a fan of this game. It's certainly unique ...

title: Alien Carnage
description: Also known as "Halloween Harry" (not sure why the name change occurred) this is one of the lesser-known titles from Apogee Software. This game features great graphics and awesome SB sound effects and music. The gameplay is very shooting oriented, similar to Duke Nukem. You also collect money to buy new weapons from vending machines. Very cool, and Apogee (now 3D Realms) has recently released the entire full version of this game as freeware! Click below to download the full version. Video ReviewVideo review of Alien Carnage, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Alien Rampage
description: Alien Rampage has no connection to either the "Alien(s)" nor the "Rampage" franchises. It's a great looking 2D platform shooting game. (But it's not Alien Carnage, a game by Apogee Software/3D Realms. Lots of games with Alien in the name!) The game's graphics and animations, as well as the abnormally large sprites including your own character, add greatly to the experience. The storyline doesn't really matter; your objective is to run through the levels, finding secrets and gathering bonuses and powerups, all while blowing away all of the enemies in your way. You do find coins which can be used to buy things. The game is rather bloody, with many enemies exploding into a bloody burst when killed.

title: Alien Trilogy
description: Alien Trilogy is a FPS based on the popular movie series that was released the same year as Quake. It is not as polished or impressive as Quake but is a great game in its own right. You play as Lt. Ripley and work your way through sections based on each of the original Alien films. You'll shoot all of the aliens you see from the movies through intricately designed space-type locations. The environments feel a bit cramped compared to Quake's more open world but there is plenty of action here, with weapons to find and many doors to activate via switches. This demo version provides the entire first level of the full game.

title: Alley Cat
description: Even though this is an extremely old game (1984!) and even though it features archaic 4-color CGA graphics, it still can be fun to play. AlleyCat has you playing an ... uh, alleycat. The object is to jump around an alley (and also inside the appartment building) trying to collect as many mice and other objects as possible while avoiding baddies like dogs, sweeping brooms (?) etc. It's neat, and besides the fact that it's a true PC gaming classic, it's amazing how much gameplay is crammed into a 32k zipfile! Video ReviewVideo review of Alleycat, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Alone In The Dark
description: Anyone who has played the Resident Evil or other modern "survival horror" games should really take a look at Alone in the Dark. It was "inspired by the work of H. P. Lovecraft". In the game, your character investigates a strange house with holds many surprises (and sometimes jump scares). It turns out, as many of you probably already know/remember, the basic mechanics used in Resident Evil were pioneered by Alone in the Dark. Its graphics, while hightech at the time of its release, look rather poor now, but remember, this was many years BEFORE 3D cards. Overall it's still a fun game to play, and the classic game that spawed the entire "survival horror" genre. (NOTES: This is the demo version of the full game. To start the game, run the file "tatou.com". Press 'S' during the game to turn on sound effects.)

title: Amazon: Guardians of Eden
description: Amazon is a graphical point-and-click adventure game using a similar engine to that seen in later Sierra and Lucasarts releases. This demo version allows you to get an idea of what the full (and apparently NOT AT ALL CHILDREN FRIENDLY) game is like. (One of the first things that will happen when you start playing is your character getting shot in the head. Fun times!) The production values are a bit cringe-worthy now but at the time having even short video clips and sound bites was pretty cool. (It also used Access Software's REALSOUND technology to play sounds through the PC speaker if you didn't have a sound card.) According to online reviews it's a decent adventure game if you can overlook a few design flaws.

title: Amulets & Armor
description: Amulets & Armor is an interesting first-person perspective RPG game that unfortunately never got much attention, presumably due to failed publishing and marketing efforts. The game attempts to combine the best elements of FPS games and RPGs, and to some degree it succeeds, having passable graphics and sounds, along with a variety of gameplay options and even multiplayer. However the game also has design problems and bugs, so it is at best a flawed unknown classic. (Note that as of 2013 the full version has been released for free as a 80meg download, see the official site to download it.) Video ReviewVideo review of Amulets & Armor, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Ant Run
description: Antrun is a great puzzle game. It's an adaption of the popular pipe-laying genre ... in this case, the task is to keep an ant running through tunnels as long as possible. You can rotate the tunnel pieces to try to keep him going. It's addicting! I was playing for about 20 minutes before I realized that I'd intended just to get a quick screenshot and write this review! :)

title: Antarctic Adventure
description: Antarctic Adventure, originally created and published by Konami, made appearances on many older video game systems, including the Colecovision, NES and MSX (among others). This is a recompiled version of the MSX game that does not require a separate emulator to play. Therefore it plays exactly like the classic game. The object is to guide your penguin to its home, avoiding obstacles and collecting bonuses (flags and fish) along the way. Smooth but unimpressive graphics will remind you of the video games of yesteryear!

title: Apples & Oranges
description: Apples & Oranges is a version of Reversi/Othello, using apples & oranges as the pieces for the two players. It works well enough since they're visually distinct. The goal is the same: Convert all of your opponent's pieces to your own. The mouse-driven interface feels natural and works well. You can also play against the CPU instead of a second player, which is a nice feature often missing from shareware programs. Also be sure to read the in-game About text for an amazing and I'm sure accurate re-telling of how the game was developed ...

title: Aqua Man
description: Aqua Man is yet another puzzle game from that master of puzzles, William Soleau of Soleau Software! (Some of which seem quite similar to each other yet are nonetheless different ...) Aqua Man is no longer mentioned on his website, which may be due it's name, which is identical to the popular DC comic character, although of course the game itself is unrelated. The game involves pushing blocks around to complete an unbroken line from the starting tile to the ending tile. Level 1 seems rather difficult, so don't expect any hand-holding easy levels to get you started! There is a level select though so you can try out other levels.

title: Aquanoid
description: A fast moving Arkanoid clone. It features VGA graphics (it's quite colorful) and PC speaker sound effects (don't worry, they can be turned off!). There are many different powerups, and one of the handy features of the game is that there is a light at the right side of the screen which tells you whether the one that's falling is good or bad, so you don't have to memorize all of the different capsules. Otherwise, very much the same as Arkanoid, so if you enjoy that game, you will probably also enjoy this knock-off. Video ReviewVideo review of Aquanoid, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Arctic Adventure
description: If you've played the classic Pharaoh's Tomb game, you'll be right at home in Arctic Adventure. The unofficial sequel to the classic platform/puzzle game, Arctic Adventure appears to use the same engine as its predecessor, and employs a similar graphical (CGA, ie 4-color) and gameplay style. Gameplay involves jumping around ice ridden levels, breaking ice with pickaxes, and trying to make your way to the exit. Apogee Software (now 3D Realms) recently released the full version of this series as freeware! Video ReviewVideo review of Arctic Adventure, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Arcy 2
description: Arcy 2 is an puzzle / action game where the object is to collect all of the keys on the level and get to the exit. Your smiley-face character needs no more storyline or motivation other than that! Similarly to the Lolo series of games, the enemies you will encounter move predictably, so although you will sometimes need quick reflexes, thinking and planning ahead are more important. The graphics and SFX are minimal but they get the job done. Thankfully the in-game help (push F1) explains what all of the different symbols are. (This game was originally shareware but has been released for free by its publisher. All three games are available in the archive, although only the first is playable online.)

title: ARK...
description: ARK... is not a great Arkanoid clone, but it was made in 1989 so we'll cut the author some slack because it does have some good qualities. It looks decent enough, even though the animation is a bit flickery and choppy. It also features mouse control which is pretty good for an 80's shareware game. The levels seem to be based off the official Arkanoid game, with some modifications. The ball bounces fast so you'd better be ready.

title: ASCII Invaders
description: ASCII Invaders is, as you might expect, an interpretation of the classic Space Invaders game using nothing but ASCII characters in text-mode. The gameplay is the same as the classic arcade game: Shoot the invaders and dodge their shots as they methodically move left and right as a group, slowly inching their way towards the bottom of the screen. (At least until the last few, when they start to speed up.) There is some animation here as well as some satisfying PC speaker sound effects. It also adds the feature of various types of "bombs" that can be used to clear away invaders, as well as removing the shields that are typically part of this sort of game. (The author notes that this game was programmed in using the Pascal programming language.)

title: Ascii Patrol
description: Ascii Patrol is a textmode version of the popular arcade classic game Moon Patrol. You pilot your moon buggy over rocky moon terrain, blowing up moon obstacles as you drive and try not to crash, all in glorious textmode! The graphics for this game are actually quite impressive given their limitations. Since the game is available for other platforms like Windows and Linux, it uses only basic text characters, not the extended DOS set. It plays pretty smoothly so definitely worth checking out. Source code is available on Github.

title: AsciiQuest
description: AsciiQuest is a game creation system (referred to in the docs as an "ascii game creation package") that I honestly haven't invested much time in learning. You can in theory create your own adventure, RPG, and puzzle games, using a collection of tools contained within the game. The game itself uses ASCII characters in Mode 13H, so you have access to 256 colors. This gives the games a unique look, but it also limits your visual options. Compared to something like ZZT, this GCS seems more difficult to learn. There is a character editor and even a music editor where you enter notes on an ASCII piano! Included in the zip file is a 20 page Microsoft Word .DOC file included to explain how things work, but it would be a challenge to get a working game running on this today since as far as I know there is no community support available. Still, an interesting and mostly unknown GCS.

title: Aspetra
description: Aspetra is a console-style RPG in the veign of classic RPGs like Dragon Quest and the older Final Fantasy games. It clearly takes influence from those sort of games in terms of style and storytelling. The story involves wizards, political (village) intrigue, and other common fantasy game themes. Battles are turn-based and result from random encounters whenever you leave town. There are plenty of weapons, armor, and items to collect, as well as baddies to battle with. If you enjoy old-school console-style RPGs this one is a polished, if not particularly unique, addition to the genre.

title: Assault Trooper
description: Assault Trooper is an isometric action game where you are sent on various military missions, such as infiltrating the enemy's base. The game looks good (although the various characters/sprites are very small so they can be tough to see) and plays fairly well. The action can get rather frantic at times and the computer controlled AI enemies seem reasonably intelligent. (Apparently the full version of this game is now freeware.)

title: Astrofire
description: Astrofire is a well-made Asteroids inspired space shooting game. It features great pre-rendered graphics, powerful sound effects, and new powerup items such as different weapons and shields. Its graphics look great and the game plays very smoothly. Definitely a fun game, even if you're tired of traditional Asteroids-type games. Although originally shareware, the developer has released the entire game as freeware! Check out their more recent games as well which expand on the Astrofire formula such as TerraFire.

title: Attack of the Petscii Robots
description: It may appear that Attack of the Petscii Robots is an action game at first glance, but it's more of a strategic game with some action elements. The goal is to destroy all of the robots in the level. To do so, first you'll need to search around and find some weapons and items. Then you'll have to use them carefully in order to defeat all the baddies. It offers numerous graphic modes to choose from and some AdLib based music. It's a fun and charming game. Definitely a unique experience, although I personally found the constant "searching" mechanic to get a bit tiresome. This is a modern game created by David Murray (aka The 8-Bit Guy of YouTube fame) and ported to many systems; this DOS port is by Jim Wright. Note that the file is 16MB but most of that is the included PDF manual, which is really nicely done but is much, much larger than all of the game files put together! (You may want to read it if you want to learn how to play, you can view it online here.) If you like the game, buy the full version at the official 8-Bit Guy website, it comes in digital download plus a variety of physical release types if you're into that.

title: Babytype
description: This typing tutorial game will help your kids to improve their typing skills. (It can also help you to become faster as well!) The various "games" are mostly just game-like visuals added on to the usual typing drills, but they can help to make the process a bit more interesting. Various difficulty levels mean that this game is appropriate for all typing skill levels, from beginner to advanced. The game also supports multiple languages including English, Russian, German and French; the default is Russian.

title: Backlash: A Turret Gunner Simulation
description: Backlash: A Turret Gunner Simulation is pretty much what its title indicates. Although its presentation in terms of its graphics, sound, menus, brief cutscenes, etc are all well done, the actual game seems to consist mostly of your space ship remaining stationary; your job is simply to blast whatever shows up on your radar. This simplifies the game's control scheme, but preventing any actual control of the ship (in favor of the "turret gunner" model as per its full name) makes you feel a bit stranded in space. The experience is thus a bit underwhelming.

title: Balloon Challenge
description: Balloon Challenge is a puzzle game with much in common with several of Soleau Software's other similar EGA/VGA puzzle games, but with some unique rules of its own. The object is to get your balloons as high as possible on the game board. After choosing a balloon, it will float up the screen, and change directions based on what it hits. So you must choose your balloons carefully! Not tremendously exciting but there is an element of strategy to the game and the playing field will be different every time that you play. Don't try to play with your friends, however, since there is no mutliplayer mode; you can only play against the computer.

title: Balloons
description: Balloons is a quick game of logic between two players or one player and the computer. The object is to take turns popping balloons while making sure to leave the last balloon for the other player. There are four different computer skill levels to choose from, and while the game is not extremely deep, games go quickly and it is presented very professionally.

title: Banyon Wars
description: Banyon Wars seems to be an earlier version of the more well-known Soleau Software game Isle Wars. The object of both games is, like the board game Risk, take over the map by warring with competing armies. You must distribute your troops and decide when to attack. Random events can alter the game as well. You play against two computer-controlled opponents (no multiplayer) in glorious CGA color, and there are seven difficulty levels to choose from. Not a bad game of its type, although the aforementioned Isle Wars is probably a better choice.

title: Barren Planet
description: Barren Planet is a modern DOS game created in CGA graphics mode. It's a turn-based strategy game, and since I am not good at strategy games at all, I'll let the developer himself describe the game (from the official website): "Players take on the role of a strategist, controlling a number of units that move around on a battle map, attacking their enemies in an attempt to control strategic locations or to wipe their opponents out altogether. A series of battles is linked together to form the full campaign, with the outcome of one battle determining what battle is fought next." You will probably want to read the Barren Planet Manual (PDF) to learn how to play!

title: Baryon
description: Baryon is a little-known shoot-em-up, created by unknown South Korean developer ACRO Studio. The gameplay is similar to most vertically scrolling shooting games, but what sets this game apart is all of the crazy action going on. There's stuff blowing up left and right, along with a rocking Soundblaster soundtrack and some impressive graphical effects. (This game uses an obscure 256x200 video mode, perhaps to allow for all its graphical trickery?) There are different powerups available, as well as two different ships you can choose, each with its own abilities. The main problem with the game is that it's sometimes quite difficult to see the bullets and other things that will kill you. But it's an impressive looking game that's fun to play. Personally I die pretty quickly but if you're a shmup fan maybe you'll actually finish the first level ... there's only one level included in the shareware version. (Run GO.EXE to start the game.)

title: Battle Arena Toshinden
description: Battle Arena Toshinden is a well-known Playstation 1 3D fighting game. It was one of the first games I bought for my PS1. It's a Tekken-style one-on-one fighting game that involves mostly hand-to-hand combat and combos. Apparently a DOS port was also made of the game, and it's better than you might think, although not the same as the PS1 version even though it shares the same characters, moves, and controls. The controls are certainly one of the trickier parts, since using the keyboard to move around in 3D while trying to remember what all of the attack / block / etc buttons do can be challenging! It runs a little slowly as well, no doubt due to doing all of its 3D work without the aid of a 3D accelerator card. An impressive technical achievement if nothing else! This demo version contains 3 characters from the full version: Eiji, Sofia, and Mondo. Apparently Earthworm Jim is also a playable character in the full version?!

title: Battle Bugs
description: Battle Bugs is a semi-real-time military strategy game of tactical insect warfare. Your mission is to eliminate the opposing team of bugs. You'll need to issue commands to your troops in a range of battle scenarios, with familiar locations like the kitchen of a home. The graphics are well done, and use the high-res (for DOS anyways) 800x600 mode. I am not personally a fan of strategy games but apparently this one is quite good. Although a total of 56 campaigns are included in the full version, this demo includes only one.

title: Battle Cheese
description: Battle Cheese is a military strategy game similar to Risk and other board games where you battle for supremacy over an area of land. The shareware version of this game is limited to either North America or Europe. Only one human player is supported in the shareware version, two in the full game. Each of the four opponents is given a section of land and automatically assigned troops at the start of the game. Then they take turns buying things, moving around, and attacking others. If you enjoy this kind of military strategy game, you may enjoy this game too. You'll also get to see a nifty title screen animation, followed by a creepy menu screen background ...

title: Battle for Atlantis
description: Battle for Atlantis is a simple war strategy game, which is similar in many ways to the popular Risk board game. Players begin with several countries, each with a different number of armies, and must war against all of the other players in an attempt to take over the board/world. There aren't a lot of special features or options here, but if you are new to this genre of game (or know someone who is) this would probably be a good choice to get them started, especially since there are multiple difficulty settings.

title: Battleship
description: Battleship is, not surprisingly, a version of the popular board game of the same name. You place your ships on a grid, and your opponent (computer, or human) takes turns trying to guess where they are located, while you take turns trying to guess where theirs are. It's a well-made game that works well and has a good "feel" to it, and emulates the experience of the board game fairly well.

title: Beast
description: Beast is a simple ASCII-based game which doesn't have much of a story, but then it doesn't really need one. Your goal is to kill each of the "beasts" on each level (big letter "H"s). However, instead of weapons, you need to use the level itself to kill them, by trapping them between the pushable walls. Since it was made in 1984 it's graphics and sounds are extremely rudimentary, but its gameplay is fairly unique although it too is pretty simple. Not bad for a 19k file! (This game was mentioned in the book "The Video Game Explosion: A History from PONG to Playstation and Beyond" by Mark J. P. Wolf.)

title: Beats Of Rage
description: If you've ever played Streets of Rage (in an arcade or for any of Sega's old home console systems) you'll know what to expect from Beats of Rage. This game aims to recreate the classic series. They have done a great job, and the game looks great. A lot of the graphics have been ripped directly from popular fighting games (not just the SoR series) and the game plays very well. There's also a Windows version of the "OpenBOR" remake available at ChronoCrash.com if the DOS version isn't working for you. (Note that the size of the .zip file for the DOS version of the game is 54megs!)

title: Beneath a Steel Sky
description: Originally a commercially released adventure game, Beneath a Steel Sky (BASS) was deemed freeware by Revolution Software in 2003. Now you can download and play it for free using the SCUMMVM software. This is a Lucasarts-style adventure game which takes place in a gritty, futuristic setting. Although the graphics and sounds are well done, some of the puzzles are a bit uninspired. Nevertheless it's clearly a well-made game and worth playing for adventure game fans. If you'd like a free pre-packaged version of the game that runs natively in Windows via the SCUMMVM engine (this is the full CD version) get the GOG.com version of Beneath a Steel Sky for free.

title: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein
description: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein is a free release of an originally commercial game which was released for free after the death of its author. ("After the death of Silas Warner in 2004, the reconstructed source code and a ported version of the game was released for free by his widow in honor of him.") The original Castle Wolfenstein of course helped inspire Wolfenstein 3D, one of the most well-known early FPS games. This is the sequel to Castle Wolfenstein, and is in fact a fan-made conversion of the PC booter to a native DOS program. It retains the complexity of the original game; see the instructions below for the myriad of keys required to play! Definitely not an easy game to jump into but I'm sure some people will enjoy it.

title: Big Rig
description: Big Rig (no relation to the laughingly bad "Big Rigs: Over the Road Racing") is a text-mode truck driving simulation game. Your job is to safely transport your cargo to the destination. Similarly to games like Oregon Trail, you are given various decisions to make as the game progresses, like how fast to drive, how much fuel to buy, or whether or not to stop at a rest stop. The game is presented entirely in text, and there are no quick reflexes required. It seems like after playing a few times, you will begin to learn the tricks of making a successful delivery. Not terribly exciting but an interesting early (1986!) simulation game.

title: Bio Menace
description: Bio Menace is a decent EGA platformer from Apogee. It's got some nice EGA graphics and SoundBlaster sounds, though, as well as a few original elements like interaction with the game's backgrounds. It has a unique style, and it encourages more thoughtful and planned playing rather than running around shooting everything. For whatever reason, however, it doesn't seem quite as fun as some of Apogee's other games. (Note that this is the full registered version of this game, which was released as freeware by 3D Realms.) Video ReviewVideo review of Bio Menace, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Black Hole
description: Black Hole is a timed puzzle game where the object is to clear all of the tiles off the screen by walking on them. According to its author Terry Cavanagh (yes, that one) it's based on a game called POD. The game is presented well and it seems like there are a lot of levels and a lot of variations on the basic gameplay which are gradually introduced as you play. The difficulty spikes up pretty rapidly with the fourth level already providing a decent challenge, especially since each level is also timed. Source code (QuickBasic) and a level editor are included. Consider buying Terry's excellent VVVVVV game and/or Terry's Other Games pack for more of his work.

title: Blackthorne
description: Although the character movement and general gameplay aesthetic may bear a strong resemblance to the classic Prince of Persia game, Blackthorne was actually developed by Blizzard Entertainment, who of course would later go on to create the wildly popular Warcraft, Starcraft, and Diablo series. In this demo version of Blackthorne you can get a taste of the full version of the game. It's an action-adventure game requiring excellent timing. The graphics and sounds are great, especially the smooth animations and stylistic world you explore. The dodging mechanic also works really well, although the complicated controls can take some getting used to. (Blizzard has made the full game available for free! Download the full version here.)

title: Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold
description: Not that bad at all. This is a game that Apogee released between Wolfenstein 3D and Rise of the Triad. Basically it uses the Wolfenstien engine with some modifications, the best of which is a map so you're not lost throughout the entire game. It also adds a greater variety of enemies, money which can be used to buy things, switches which change the level, and so on. It isn't quite as memorable as Wolf3D (mostly because it lacks the freshness of that game) but if you like the older 3D games like Wolf3D or Catacomb Abyss you might want to try it out. Video ReviewVideo review of Blake Stone, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Blam! Machinehead
description: Blam! Machinehead is a first-person shooting game where you pilot a hovercraft around a strange world. Not sure what the story is but basically you seem to fly around and blast robotic bugs (?!) while activating bases to get keys to do ... things? I probably could've researched this more but it's also probably unnecessary. The game looks flashy and has a lot of whirring and buzzing sound effects, so it's worth trying out just for that, but it feels so much less cohesive than DOOM or something. At least it defaults to mouselook aiming, important for taking out those flying bugs.

title: Block-Man
description: Block-Man is the original Block Man game, preceding the more well-known Block Man II. The gameplay is much the same, except with even plainer graphics. The game also ranks your intelligence after completing each level, from "Brainless" all the way to "Super Genius". After completing level one, you're ranked "Vegetable" with the representative member being "A cucumber". Thanks, game! Anyways there are a total of 10 puzzles here (in the shareware version) involving carrying and placing blocks, if that's your thing. See the FILE_ID.DIZ below for the inane and unnecessary story for the game!

title: Blockout
description: Blockout is one of the best Tetris sequel that is not an official Tetris release. It's basically Tetris in 3D. Instead of looking at the well from the side, you look down into it, and rotate and place all of the pieces in 3D. It's a bit tricky to get used to, but many consider this game one of the definitive (albeit unofficial) iterations of the original Tetris formula. Welltris is the official 3D version and honestly I'm not sure how they differ, but Blockout seems to be the better known of the two. (This game has been released by permission of Kadon Enterprises Inc (who are copyright holders of the Blockout name) on the Blockout.net website. Visit the Kadon website GamePuzzles.com for many interesting and fun puzzle games.) There is also an online version with a global high scores board by Magnus Ivarsson available at Blockout.nu.

title: Blood
description: Made using the "Build" 3D engine (the same engine used to make Duke Nukem 3D), Blood is an often overlooked game that is actually quite well made and offers plenty of fun for 3D shooting fans. This demo version includes an introduction to the full game. Not surprisingly, this game serves up a lot of ... uh, blood. And severed heads, and so on ... plus lots of frantic 3D action. (NOTE: It should be obvious but this game is not intended for children!) Video ReviewVideo review of Blood, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Blupi at Home
description: Blupi at Home (the character is also sometimes referred to as Eggbert in English-speaking countries) is a game based around the French character Blupi. It's a game primarily for young children (3-8 are the recommended ages) based primarily around exploration. You use the mouse to click things around Blupi's house, and he will perform some action with them and also spell out the word for you to read. There are some minigames to discover as well. It's sort of charming but I doubt that most kids who are old enough to confidently use the mouse in the way necessary to play this would be too interested in it. This game was originally released commercially but has since been made freely available by its developers in 2017. Visit the official Blupi website here for more free Blupi games. Thanks goes to Mr Fibble of DOS Games Archive for preparing this re-pack which works easily in DOSBox.

title: Body Blows
description: Body Blows is a one-on-one fighting game that seems to aim to approximate the aesthetic and experience of games like Street Fighter II. However, it is not nearly as refined as those games. It looks good visually, but the game itself (and it's "interesting" control scheme) doesn't play very well. In this demo version, you control Nik (a generic fighting guy) and fight against yourself. If you're able to figure out the controls (see below or the included README.DOC file) you will still probably have a bad time unless you remember this game fondly from your youth!

title: Bolo Adventures I
description: Bolo Adventures is an EGA puzzle game which feels much in line with other Soleau Software puzzle games. This game is one of the many variants of Sokoban, where the main object is to push blocks around to escape each level / screen. There have been many additions to the gameplay to add more variety to the levels, such as different kinds of pushable blocks, enemies, and obstacles like lasers and water. (Rescue Rover came to mind for some reason while playing Bolo Adventures, probably due to the lasers.) Graphically the game is rather plain with simple EGA sprites to depict each object. There are 20 levels in this shareware version versus the 40 in total that you get in the registered version.

title: Bolo Adventures III
description: Bobo Adventures III is basically the same game as the first

title: Bolo Ball
description: Bolo Ball is a simple but interesting strategy game intended for one player vs the computer. (There doesn't seem to be a multiplayer option.) The object is to strategically choose which of your 29 balls to push down the playing field. The farther your ball bounces down, the more points you get. As the playing field changes during the game, your decisions may become less obvious. It's a fun and fairly unique little game, with the usual Soleau Software style EGA graphics and basic PC speaker sound effects.

title: BombAway
description: BombAway is similar to Tank Wars, Scorched Earth, and all of the rest of the turn-based artillery-firing games. Set your angle and velocity, and hope you are able to dial it in before your opponent does! This game is two-player only, and lacks some of the bells and whistles that later games provided. You must hit your opponent RIGHT in the CENTER of their tank in order for your shot to count, so it may look like you hit your opponent, but you'll need to adjust your settings ever so slightly to actually make it count.

title: BrainStorm Pro
description: BrainStorm Pro is a gravity-based piece-matching game which bears similarity in its gameplay to the Epic Megagames classic game Brix. Both seem inspired by Taito's Puzznic game, although Brix was an obvious clone / rip-off, whereas BrainStorm Pro has its own style while retaining similar gameplay. The goal is to match up all the pieces, using your mouse to click and drag them as they fall downwards. Different environmental blocks can affect how your other blocks move or exhibit their own unique properties to deal with. A decent game with 20 levels available in the shareware version.

title: Brutal: Paws of Fury
description: Brutal: Paws of Fury is a one-on-one fighting game in the style of Street Fighter and other similar fighting games from the 90's. Unlike most games of this style, the game has a cutesy-serious tone (is that a thing?) with anthropomorphic animals as its martial-artist protagonists. One advantage is that it's not too violent, so it'll be okay for younger kids to play it. The graphics are decent, with fast but not particularly smooth animations. As with most PC fighting games, doing the special moves (if you even know them) will be a challenge with the keyboard. The demo version offered here only provides two of the characters available in the full game.

title: Bust-a-Move 2: Arcade Edition
description: Bust-a-Move (aka Puzzle Bobble) is an extremely popular series of bubble-matching games which combine a puzzle game's need for strategy with the quick-thinking and reflexes needed for success in an action game. It is popular in arcades as well as home consoles. This demo of Bust-a-Move 2 allows you to experience this conversion of the arcade game for DOS, albeit with no music and limited levels. The object is to shoot colored balls towards the top of the screen, aiming to match three or more to clear them from the board. You can also bounce 'em off the walls. Once the screen is clear, you move to the next board. Nice graphics and of course the loveable Bub & Bob from the Bubble Bobble games make an appearance.

title: C-Dogs
description: The sequel to Cyberdogs, C-Dogs improves the original Cyberdogs gameplay formula in some ways. The game involves you taking your character on missions which usually involve shooting anything around using a variety of weapons that can be bought before missions. Many more options are available in this version, one of the most interesting being an editor that allows you to create your own C-Dogs campaigns. An open source port was later released which is still being added to and improved, available here: C-Dogs SDL Port Video ReviewVideo review of C-Dogs, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Cannon Fodder
description: Cannon Fodder is an action-oriented strategy game where you control a team of up to six soldiers on various missions. Use the mouse to move your team and fight your enemies on the way to completing your objectives. The game has decent graphics, although since it's a Sensible Software title the characters are rendered as tiny sprites on the screen! While not as in-depths as most strategy titles or as action-packed as many of the best action games, Cannon Fodder's hybrid gameplay landed it as one of the "1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die" book. The full game has 72 levels of combat, although this version is the "shareware" version (re)published by MVP Software has significantly less. Video ReviewVideo review of Cannon Fodder, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Captain Comic
description: One of my first experiences with 'shareware' way back a couple of months before we'd even purchased our old 2400baud modem ... Anyways, this game was quite innovative back when it was released, with it's smooth scrolling EGA graphics and sound effects. (This was 1989, of course.) It's still a pretty cool game; the enemies and locations are memorable, as is the music. (At the time I didn't know that the Captain Comic theme song is actually a rendition of the United States Marine Corps Hymn.) The main thing it lacks is a save feature ... which means you'll just have to spend hours at a time trying to finish it. :) Video ReviewVideo review of Captain Comic, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Capture the Flag
description: This game was given several glowing reviews upon its initial release (1994/95) and its easy to see why. This shareware game has an interface that is very professionally done and rivals the commercial games of its time. The graphics are clean and functional, and overall the game is very well designed. This is a clever turn-based strategy game where the object is to capture the other team's flag. Multiplayer play is supported, via hotseat (same computer), modem or PBEM (Play By EMail).

title: Carmageddon
description: This demo version of the formerly popular car racing / gore game give you a taste of what the full game had to offer; and for many it will be enough! :) Unlike most racing games, this one actually rewards you for damaging the other cars (you get more money at the end of the race depending on how much damage you cause). You can also run over pedestrians. (No bonuses for that!) The games graphics were pretty good for their time, and the controls handle reasonably well. (This game is VIOLENT and INAPPROPRIATE for children so if you are under 18 years old please get your parent's permission before downloading.) Video ReviewVideo review of Carmageddon, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Castle Adventure
description: This is a very old "graphic" adventure game which uses textmode / ASCII characters. Despite its simplicity, there is something charming about its gameplay, and it is nostalgically remembered by gamers who played it in the DOS era. Many adventure games back in 1985 were still text based, so having any kind of visual representation would no doubt be welcomed. Anyways, the game itself is rather average, but it does include action and adventure elements, although there is very little plot. It plays sort of like a Kroz-type ASCII game mixed with a text adventure. A modern Windows remake is available here by Chris Benshoof and is likely a better way to play this game these days!

title: Cavern of the Evil Wizard
description: If you've ever seen the Tom Hanks movie Big (1988) you'll probably remember a PC graphical adventure game that is shown briefly. It's identified as "Cavern of the Evil Wizard", but to the disappointment of many fans of the movie, it was just made up for the movie; it didn't actually exist. Now a developer has made his own interpretation of the game, based on the screens seen in the movie. It keeps the same CGA graphic aesthetic and text-based input. Although you know how the game ends, you'll now get to see how the hero got there! Very cool since I remember Googling this when I got the Internet long ago and being disappointed that it wasn't a real game. Well, here it is, the full game for your enjoyment! Thank you MontieMongoose! (A Windows executable is also included but running the DOS version is recommended by the author.) I recently learned that this game is an expansion of a previously developed game by BoMToons, so check out the archived site for some more history about it.

title: CD-Man
description: One of the earliest (and most famous) attempts to modernize the classic Pacman game. As with most Pac-Man type games, there is no real story, just collect the pellets and avoid the enemies. This variant features wonderfully drawn EGA graphics, innovative gameplay elements (gates & keys) and it generally plays very well. Each stage has its own surprises! (The version listed here is v1.5 which most people will likely remember, with the Pac-Man looking main character and only 2.5 finished levels. There is also a v2.0 with a different main character and more levels, but the legality of distributing that version is questionable.) Video ReviewVideo review of CD-Man, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: CHAMP Kong
description: An excellent conversion of the old arcade classic. If you've never played the original, this was the introduction of Mario (then called "Jumpman") and the gameplay consists of a variety of platforming levels where the goal is to rescue Pauline from the great ape. It features great graphics, sweet SB sound (taken directly from the arcade!) and lots of other nice, professional touches. Overall ... it's a great recreation of the arcade, which also includes a "CHAMP" mode with additional content.

title: CHAMP Ms Pac-Em
description: Ms Pac-Em works well as a companion to the original Pac-Em. And by "original" I mean the first game released, not original in the sense of being unique since it's a near-clone of the classic Pac-Man game. This version is of course a clone of Ms Pac-Man, and it thus offers the differing maze layouts and other improvements offered by the sequel to the original maze-munching arcade game. It offers the same great graphics and gameplay as Pac-Em and the Ms Pac-Man arcade game, so if you enjoy either, definitely try this version as well. (As usual, I am not a big Pac-Man aficionado, so I don't know whether the ghost movements are exactly accurate or not!)

title: CHAMP Pac-Em
description: Pac-Em is a great clone of the classic Pac-Man arcade game. In case you've never played Pac-Man (!?) the object is to eat the dots and avoid the ghosts; that is, unless you collect a power pellet, in which case, the tables are turned and it's your chance to chase the ghosts! This is a very accurate version of the arcade version of the game, as far as I can tell. (I'm no expert so I don't know if the ghosts move entirely accurately.)

title: Charlie II
description: Charlie II is the sequel to Wiering Software's "Charlie the Duck". As such, it's similar to the original game. Very similar, in fact. It seems to use the same engine, and shares a lot of graphical touches and gameplay devices. The object of the game is to guide your duck through various Mario-like side-scrolling levels, collecting coins and gems. The graphics and sounds are still quite decent and the game flows quite well, although the way the action scrolls can be a bit tricky at times.

title: Charlie the Duck
description: As soon as you run this game, you can tell it's going to be an experience that's higher quality than your average shareware game. The VGA graphics in this sidescrolling Mario-esque jumping game are very nice, and there are some SB sound effects too. (Unfortunately no music.) The gameplay consists of just getting to the next level. Probably influenced by the Great Giana Sisters (which itself was highly "influenced" by Mario). Charlie the Duck is quite fun to play, although unforgiving, so plan your jumps carefully!

title: Chasm: The Rift
description: This surprisingly good 3D shooting game (the demo is downloadable here) is, in terms of technical things like graphics, somewhere between DOOM and Quake. Unlike most other 3D copycat-style games of this time period, this game actually plays quite decently. There is an actual story before the game begins, and once the game starts there is plenty of frantic action, along the lines of Quake. Recommended!

title: Chesshousers
description: Chesshousers is an interesting and visually eye-catching puzzle game. The goal is to direct your player (a glove) through an isometic-perspective maze. You have no weapons, all you can do is move around and push/destroy certain objects. Chess pieces move as the do in the chess board game (ex, pawns move straight ahead) and you'll need to carefully think through their movement before you push them to progress. The graphics look great but the isometric viewpoint sometimes makes it unnecessarily difficult to see what's going on. (There is a helpful list of objects in the game and what they do on the Mobygames description.)

title: Chex Quest
description: Based on a modified version of the DOOM engine, Chex Quest was originally included on free promotional CDs with General Mills Chex brand cereal. Surprisingly, this game is actually decent, with fairly good graphics and sounds (not too surprising, given its DOOM-based engine). Although it's fairly short (only five levels) its surreal atmosphere makes it worth trying out. (Also Chex Quest 3 for Windows was released, and is now officially being promoted by General Mills. Nice!)

title: Chompsters
description: A very fun Pacman type game that expands on the original Pacman idea by adding different characters (Pacmen?) to play, as well as having varied, large levels and ghosts with individual personalities that talk to you between levels. The levels actually scroll so you can't see the entire playing area at once. Your Pacman can also jump and use new special items. With the scrolling playing field and jumping, it seems influenced by Pacmania. It's all very well done, and it's fun to play, as well.

title: Clockwiser
description: Clockwiser is an inventive and now free puzzle game. Originally a commercial product, the game has graciously been released for free by its original developers. Racing against the clock, you must draw rectangles and rotate blocks clockwise (or counter-clockwise) to make the blocks on the left side of the screen match the blocks on the right side. It includes over 200 levels and later levels introduce new mechanics, like gravity, teleporters, and bombs. The game plays quite well (you can use keyboard or mouse, the latter of which is recommended) and looks good too. Definitely a hidden gem that you should try out. The main disadvantage is that you'll need to use the copy-protection sheet included in the ZIP file (Clockwiser load-up matrix) to solve the copy protection challenge.

title: Cochese
description: A pushing puzzle game, where you must collect various "bad" things (drugs, needles, etc.) and get to the exit within a certain number of moves. The graphics are fairly average MCGA fare, and there's no sound effects, but it could be enjoyable nonetheless. (Note: The game has a strong anti-drug message.)

title: CoffeeBreak Card Games
description: CoffeeBreak Card Games is a shareware game that is probably a bit too limited to entice people to spend the $30US (approximately $55US in today's money!) to buy the full game, despite the decent production values displayed here. The shareware version includes two card games: 52 Pickup and Crazy 8s. Both play decently enough, and thankfully there is a bit more strategy to 52 Pickup than the version my dad had me play back in the day! In any case, the other four games are only available upon registration, which is unfortunately no longer possible. You may want to also check out other card games on DOSGames.com.

title: Colossal Cave Adventure
description: This is a bit before my time ... however, it's worth playing at least once, just to see one of the first text adventure games ever created. It was originally authored by Will Crowther in 1976, then expanded in 1977 with the help of Don Woods. In it you must type in commands to move through various locations and solve puzzles. This game inspired the ZORK series of games and thousands of others. (This is a 350 points version of the game. For lots more info on this game, plus dozens of other versions of the game for DOS and many other platforms, visit Baf's Interactive Fiction Guide: Adventure!)

title: Commander Keen 1: Invasion of the Vorticons
description: This is the first game (the shareware one) in the original Commander Keen series, "Commander Keen in Invasion of the Vorticons". (This episode's subtitle is "Marooned on Mars".) I thought that this game was SO amazing when I first played it (many years ago), and it's still quite fun now. It features great graphics (for EGA) and some not-so-annoying PC speaker sound effects. At the time, it was quite innovative due to the way that the screen smoothly scrolls. The engine was originally pitched to Nintendo for a PC Mario game, but since that never happened, Commander Keen was born to make use of it. The jumping and pogo-sticking (yes, that's a word) take a bit of getting used to ... otherwise, a great, classic Apogee platformer which spawned numerous sequels and an unofficial "mascot" for this website. :) Video ReviewVideo review of Commander Keen, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Commander Keen 4: Secret of the Oracle
description: Commander Keen Secret of the Oracle is the well-received fourth episode in the Commander Keen series. (The series this game is part of is called "Goodbye Galaxy!") Like the original game, it was developed by iD Software and published by Apogee. In this game, Billy "Commander Keen" Blaze is again called into action and must adventure into an overhead map and then into platforming stages. The main complaint against this game (as with the original) would probably the one-hit-death mechanics, which can make each level feel more stressful as you near the exit! However this game improves on the graphics, music, and sound effects of the earlier games while including many of the same elements that made the original successful (such as the pogo stick) and provides a fun experience. (It even includes an epic game of Pong, aka "Paddle War", on the main menu ...)

title: Commander Keen 6: Aliens Ate My Babysitter
description: This demo (3 playable levels) version of the 6th episode in the popular Commander Keen series continues the adventures Keen began in the 4th episode of the series. The engine and most of the enemies, powerups, etc are the same, except with all new level designs. Since the basic game is the same, if you enjoy the other Keen games, you'll probably like this one. If you're new to the series, this is a good place to start. (Although there are only three levels in the demo; try Commander Keen 4: Secret of the Oracle for a complete game with the same style.)

title: Commander Keen: Keen Dreams
description: Keen Dreams is sometimes referred to as Keen 3.5, because it was made between the first trilogy of Keen games and Commander Keen 4: Secret of the Oracle. Originally published by Softdisk as a commercially released game, at some point they also made a shareware version. This game plays in some ways like an early test game for what would become the next series of Keen games. Unlike the other games where you have a blaster and pogo stick, here you collect stones (?) which you throw at various food-related enemies in order to stun them. The gameplay is quite similar to the later games, and the graphics are similar too (although more simplistic). Most disturbing perhaps is the fact that there is no music (at least in the shareware release) even though there is a menu option for it! (Apparently it was removed in order to fit the game onto a 360k floppy disk!) Still enjoyable to play however.

title: Corridor 7: Alien Invasion
description: This game was unfortunately released shortly after Doom, meaning that it had to compete with one of the best 3D shooters of all time using ... the Wolfenstein 3D engine. Not even a fair fight, really. While the game is decent enough, its pretty obvious that its using the Wolf3D engine, with its boxy environments and simple sprites. Overall, it has decent graphics (again, comparable to Wolf3D), and it could be enjoyable if you force yourself to forget about Doom and play this game based on its own merits.

title: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure
description: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure is one of Apogee's great EGA sidescrollers. Having been apparently abandoned by his parents, Cosmo must ... well, the story doesn't really matter here. This game plays similarly to Commander Keen, as you must platform your way through the levels. There is no world map here, you simply progress from one level to the next. Cosmo has some added abilities, however, like using his suction-cupped hands to grab onto walls to climb. One of the lesser-known Apogee classics, although the framerate is lower than other comparable games of the time (apparently due to the parallax scrolling). Video ReviewVideo review of Cosmo, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Crayon Box
description: Crayon Box is intended for primary school aged children, and provides a coloring book as well as several other entertainment / edutainment modes. Almost everything is handled via the mouse (except input of numbers etc) and although the menu is a bit confusing (kids may need some help navigating) it offers several activities such as a counting game and quiz to identify the various states of the United States. The main disappointing parts of the program is that it only comes with two (!) pictures to color, and there are annoying registration nag screens. Other than that it's pretty solid as a whole although no particular part is very remarkable.

title: Crazy Drake
description: Crazy Drake is a duck / superhero who clearly is aspiring to be Earthworm Jim. The SNES / Genesis game starring an Earthworm (which was later ported to many other systems, even DOS!) was clearly an inspiration for this game. Crazy Drake moves much like Earthworm Jim, and like him has a gun with unlimited ammo. The levels have great graphics and nice animations. Again like Earthworm Jim, there are various entertaining gameplay elements scattered around, like riding balloons over a shark pit. The game controls generally well, and the music is repetitive but catchy. I hate to keep comparing the two, but they're so similar in style that if you like Earthworm Jim, you'll probably like this one too. (Note: When playing in-browser, the keyboard arrow keys may not work entirely correctly, ex trying to shoot up/left. If this is the case for you, try using the numeric keypad instead if your keyboard has one.)

title: Crazy Eights
description: Crazy Eights is a simple but fun card game. This version pits you against the computer in a 1-vs-1 battle. Unfortunately there is no 2-player mode. However the game is presented in a very slick way, and the computer automatically does some things for you to make the gameplay progress smoothly. Overall a nice-looking, simple card game.

title: Crime Fighter
description: Crime Fighter shares a couple of things in common with the popular Grand Theft Auto series ... at least in terms of style. Despite the name, you don't do much crime fighting here since you play a recently released criminal on a crime binge. Unlike GTA, this is primarily a strategy game, where you explore the town and commit crimes, interspersed with some puzzles or simple minigames. Overall, it's an interesting game which provides a lot of variety ... just don't try any of this stuff in real life! Video ReviewVideo review of Crime Fighter, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Cross of Insanity
description: Cross of Insanity is a puzzle game where the object is to group all of the colored blocks with their same colors. In other words, after the colors are scrambled, they must be placed back as you can see them in the screenshot, although the positions of the color blocks can be different. Sort of like Rubik's Cube, but not. You move the colors around by rotating the vertical ring of colors, or the horizontal ring of colors, using the function keys. It's a difficult game and must take a lot of time and patience to win, which I obviously don't have!

title: Crystal Caves
description: An interesting (although in many ways average) EGA sidescroller created by Apogee right around the same time as the first Keen game was released, which may help explains why it has been generally overlooked. In any case, it's nowhere near being a bad game, so if you're looking for a good EGA platformer, try it out. It seems to share the same engine as the Secret Agent games, also from Apogee. Note that it can be annoying at times, with one-hit deaths and sometimes unfair level layouts. NEW! Read my review of the 2020 re-release Crystal Caves HD! Available on Steam and GOG.com.

title: Cyberbox 2
description: If you enjoyed the original Cyberbox puzzle game, you will probably also enjoy Cyberbox 2. The sequel features the same sort of puzzles that made the original popular. In fact, it features LOTS more puzzles. :) The action involves sliding boxes of different types in order to complete the level's objectives. The graphics/sounds of course are extremely outdated but for puzzle fans this might still be a fun diversion.

title: Cybersphere
description: One of many Arkanoid clones, this one is fairly average. It is a bit more challenging than most Arkanoid games, however, because the ball moves very quickly and since the blocks are close to the bottom of the screen, you have little time to react. VGA graphics and some nice SB effects. The music can be rather repetitive. (This game was released for free by its author, Clay Hellman.) Video ReviewVideo review of Cybersphere, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Cybersphere Plus
description: Cybersphere Plus seems to use the same engine as the original Arkanoid-like Cybersphere game but includes a new collection of levels to play. The design of the levels seems a little more forgiving than the original game, but otherwise, most of the game is the same except for the new levels. There are still explosions and other fun things going on, and the mouse-based controls work pretty well for an Arkanoid-type game. (This game was released for free by its author, Clay Hellman.)

title: D/Generation
description: D/Generation is a unique isometic view action/puzzle game set in a large office building. You play a package delivery guy who gets trapped within the Genoq Biolabs facility when the security system goes berserk. The excellent graphics and playing style are both quite unique and the game's mix of puzzle and action gameplay work well together. (Tip: Press Alt-K to "rotate" the arrow keys 45 degrees to better facilitate isometic mode.) Clever touches abound, such as the computer terminals you find which explain parts of the story, and the weird things that people say when you rescue them. Clearly a lot of time and loving care went into crafting this game. This demo version gives you a preview of what the full game has to offer.

title: Dangerous Dave
description: Before creating Keen, Wolfenstein, and Doom, John Romero was programming small games for SoftDisk, which back then included some kind of games club. (I remember vaguely seeing the ads in gaming magazines back in the late 80's/early 90's). This game is cool basically only because of the author. ;) Otherwise, it's an rather average (and, at times, quite annoying) VGA jumping game / tech demo. (This game was titled "Dangerous Dave in the Deserted Pirate's Hideout! " on the Apple II, but the DOS version is simply titled "Dangerous Dave".) Video ReviewVideo review of Dangerous Dave, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Dangerous Dave in Copyright Infringement
description: This is not so much a game as it is a tech demo, but what a tech demo it was back in 1990. Future id Software superstar John Carmack created a way to have smooth scrolling EGA graphics, which was a brand new thing back then. Together with Tom Hall they put together a quick demo to showcase the new technology which was dubbed "Dangerous Dave in Copyright Infringement". See this article by John Romero about the game for more information about the game's development. (Or the great book Masters of Doom about the history of id Software.) It's not much fun as a GAME (there's only one "level", no enemies, the question mark blocks don't work ...) but it's still very neat to play as a piece of video game history, or even as a parody of sorts of the classic NES Mario games. (It also includes the TED level editor that Romero created.)

title: Daymare 1
description: Daymare I is a first-person perspective dungeon crawler, and the original game upon which its better known sequel Daymare 2 is based. There is not much story given; you simply roll your character and proceed into the maze. Unlike the sequel, there is no auto-map, so navigation can be tricky. However the game is still quite easy to get the hang of, and it doesn't seem to punish new players with excruciating difficulty like many games in the PC dungeon-crawler genre.

title: DBQuest
description: DBQuest is seemingly the most well-known game created using the DCGames game creation system. It is an RPG that includes 256-color graphics and a large world to explore, with 75 NPCs to talk with and a large number of areas to traverse. You begin at your own home, and quickly find the castle nearby with the king & queen inside, who give you a quest to find an amulet to save their ill son. Typical RPG fare. Monsters are visible on the map, where you also fight them without transitioning to a separate battle screen. The graphics align pretty closely to the Ultima games.

title: DC Games Graphics Adventure Game Builder
description: DCGames is an Ultima-style RPG game creation system. Users of this system created numerous DOS RPGs such as DBQuest and Rescue of Lorri in Lorrinitron.The system itself seems rather complicated to learn, with many hotkeys, subscreens, and extensive reading of the documentation required. However, as the games noted above demonstrate, for those with the patience to learn it, you can create some decent games. The linked download is v4.0; see the extra files for the upgrade patches. (Currently the v4.06 to v4.07 patch is missing, please let me know if you have it.)

title: Death Rally
description: Top-down racing games are sort of a sub-genre of the larger racing genre, and Death Rally is a good example of how to do things right. Sort of like Super Sprint with more destruction. The graphics are great, as are the sounds, and the gameplay involves picking up or buying cool weapons to destroy the other cars in the races (hence the name). One of Apogee's later products, this game has all the markings of Apogee's other quality games.

title: Deluxe Ski Jump
description: Deluxe Ski Jump is a great ski jump simulation game. The game's sequels are still continuing to this day, ie Deluxe Ski Jump 4 on the author's website. The original DOS version of the game isn't in 3D like the modern versions but it's still fun and well done, albeit simple since you're doing basically the same thing every time. Using the mouse, begin your jump, time your leap from the end of the take-off board and then carefully adjust in the air before performing your landing. It takes a few tries to get right but it's not too difficult. The shareware version includes four different jump locations.

title: Descent
description: Descent was quite popular on its release. It expanded on the 3D shooting genre by giving players a real 3D environment unlike Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. In this 7-level DEMO version of Descent you must pilot your spaceship through many 3D levels destroying various bad guys along the way. Think of Doom crossed with Wing Commander and you'll have a fairly good picture of what this game's about. A fun shooter that has aged pretty well (and still works on my XP computer) that lacks a bit of the flair and style of Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. Video ReviewVideo review of Descent, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Descent II
description: The sequel to the awesome original Descent game, this game picks up right where the first left off. You again fly your ship with full range of movement around the many mine shafts destroying enemy robots. There are of course new enemies to fight and new features like the Guide-bot. The engine used seems the same engine used in the original game with some minor additions, but the graphics look a little better and it still plays quite well and runs smoothly ... at least in DOSBox, not sure about hardware back when it was released in 1996! A great game and worthy sequel, despite the sometimes motion-sickness inducing movements. There are three levels to try in this demo version. Video ReviewVideo review of Descent 2, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Desert Storm Command
description: Desert Storm Command is actually like two different games in one. Or maybe one game with two different modes. You are tasked with protecting your comrade troops, first by shooting enemy soldiers in windows, then by shooting down enemy missiles and planes "Missile Command"-style. The graphics are decent enough for the time period, and the action is certainly frantic. You'll be clicking almost continually with the mouse, since you don't seem to have any ammo to worry about. While there are the two different modes which alternate each level, the game does feel much the same throughout, and the levels also feel a bit too long.

title: Destruction Derby
description: Destruction Derby plays pretty much as you would expect: Crash your car into your opponents' cars, trying to cause as much damage to them as possible, while avoiding damage yourself. The game is presented in a rather impressive 3D mode which rivals the graphics of the early Playstation game console. (Not too surprising, I guess, since the game was also released for PS1 and other systems. It was even included on the recently released, poorly received Playstation Classic console.) The gameplay seems fun enough but, based on this limited demo, might not have a lot of depth to it. But it's definitely impressive to see it running smoothly in DOSBox.

title: Digger Remastered
description: Quite similar to the classic games DigDug and Mr.Do, this game gained some sort of PC gaming cult status. I had a couple of requests for this one since starting the site, so I figured I'd better add it. It plays well, offers lots of command line options, and you can turn off the music! (It's not that bad for PC speaker music, but after playing games and listening to MODs for so long, I've grown rather tired of the "Popcorn" song.) The graphics are nicely done in CGA, and overall it's a fun game to play. (Technically this is a reverse-engineered version of the original Windmill Software game, released for free by Andrew Jenner.)

title: Digital League Baseball
description: Digital League Baseball is a baseball simulation game, meaning that you get to manage the team but don't actually get to play. You choose your team, determine the starting lineup, and make substitutions during the game. Other than that, you watch as the computer generates random numbers and compares them against the stats of the players.
