This game has a graphical view that shows the field, and animations when things are happening, so that's a nice touch given how old the game is. It also includes all of the actual teams and players from the time (no doubt unlicensed from the MLBPA) so that's also pretty neat.

title: Dinosaur Predators
description: Dinosaur Predators is essentially a reskin of Animal Quest, the better-known game in this short-lived series of strategic animal simulations. The object is to move your chosen dinosaur around the grid, eating food and avoiding predators. The full game includes four different episodes: "Jurassic Dinosaurs," "Terror in the Swamp," "Oviraptor Egg Thief," and "Ice Age Mammals." (The shareware only includes the first.) Probably more fun than Animal Quest for kids that are heavily into dinosaurs!

title: Disney's Aladdin
description: This demo version of the wonderfully animated game based on the 1992 Disney movie Aladdin (sometimes misspelled Alladin) gives you a taste of what the full game offers. You of course play Aladdin, and you must platform your way through many levels based on scenes from the iconic movie, including the bazaar, caves, and palace. As you might expect from a Disney-based game, the graphics, sounds, and MOD-like music are great, and the controls are responsive and work well for this type of game. It doesn't feel like a forced movie-based cash-in game, but rather a natural extension of the world created by the popular movie.

title: Disney's Beauty and the Beast: Be Our Guest
description: Beauty and the Beast consists of a series of puzzle-type mini games based loosely on the Disney movie adaptation. One of the seven games is playable in this demo version. The goal in this game is to help direct the eggs into the pan at the bottom of the screen by interacting with various objects on the shelves. It's much trickier than it looks, and one mistake can result in a broken egg. (See the YouTube video if you want to see what the minigames are like that aren't included in the demo.) The game does feature good graphics and music (digital renditions of songs from the movie) as you would expect from a Disney title.

title: DOOM
description: Chosen by Computer Gaming World as part of their 'Hall of Fame' ("DOOM revolutionized PC action games"), and at (or near) the top of many "best of" game lists, DOOM is one of the most played computer games of all time. And for good reason! I admit, it scared the hell outta me when I first played it. Even today, with increasingly sophisticated 3D action games DOOM's gameplay is classic. Get it now, even if you've already played it ... it's still fun. But just in case you've never played it before (play it now!) this game was revolutionary because of both its technical prowess and its amazing game design by a team of supremely talented developers at id Software. You play as a space marine who needs to shoot up a bunch of demons and stuff. (Not the "official" storyline but pretty much all you need to know.) The game has an amazing "feel" that leads to people still playing it enthusiastically even today. It helped that a huge modding community started making new maps for it, and even total conversions. The game just celebrated its 25th birthday as of December 2018! Video ReviewVideo review of DOOM, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: DOOM 2D
description: DISCLAIMER: First of all, if you're looking for the real 3D DOOM game from id Software, the game on this page is not by id Software and certainly not endorsed by them! (This is a sort of parody of the original DOOM.) Get the REAL original DOOM game here.Now then ... DOOM 2D is a strange experiment / parody (?) of the actual game. It was created by a Russian programming team and as you might expect, attempts to recreate the DOOM experience in a 2D platforming environment. It uses graphics and sound effects ripped from the official game. The controls are not bad, and there must have been considerable work that went into making it, with many different enemies, items, traps, even bosses and a two-player simultaneous mode. That said, I don't find it to be tremendously fun to play, so it seems to exist more for its novelty than anything else. (If you speak Russian, you may be interested in the included level editor. If not, it'd take considerable trial and error to figure out how it works!)

title: Doom The Roguelike
description: Making the famous DOOM 3D shooting game into a RogueLike, turn-based RPG game with text "graphics" sounds like the recipe for disaster. But this RPG based on the original DOOM games (actually referred to as DRL, I suppose due to copyright concerns) actually plays very well. While more simplistic than games like Nethack or ADOM, DRL focuses more on combat (of course!) and weaponry, so it is faster paced than more traditional RogueLike games. Quite innovative and surprisingly good, a definite must-play for fans of the text-based RPG subgenre. (There are also more recent releases available for Windows, Linux, and OSX on the official site.)

title: Double Pacman
description: Double Pacman is a well-done rendition of the arcade classic game with the added feature of offering two-player simultaneous play. The game looks very similar to the original, and offers both cooperative and competitive modes of play. As expected, you eat dots, collect power pellets, and avoid ghosts. If you have a second player (and can stand sharing the keyboard with them) the game takes on a whole other level of gameplay. The game was made in 1994 but seems to have only been released recently by its author, and the Turbo Pascal 5 source code is also available from the author.

title: DreamWeb
description: Dreamweb is an unusual fully overhead perspective graphical adventure game. This dystopian future game has you playing as Ryan, a bartender, who has been suffering from nightmares, and eventually is drawn into a strange quest to become "the deliverer" and destroy the DreamWeb. While like other graphical adventure games you collect items and use them to solve puzzles, the viewpoint here is entirely overhead, which is an interesting switch but it provides certain challenges, like not always being able to see things clearly. To help overcome this the game does provide mouseover descriptions of items and a small "zoomed in" window in the lower corner. Definitely an intriguing and not too well known game. (This game was made freeware by its authors, as per the enclosed license.txt file.) Video ReviewVideo review of DreamWeb, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Drug Wars: A Game Based on the New York Drug Market
description: Written by a high school student and sometimes referred to as the "original GTA", the game has really nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto, and more to do with a stock market type simulation game that happens to have the theme of a drug dealer. In the game, you are given $2,000, and you need to buy and sell drugs to turn that into at least $5,500 to pay off your debt. As you move to different areas, time progresses, random events may occur, and the prices of the drugs changes. The game is presented in a distinct text mode system in monochrome, so you'll have to use your imagination. This game served as the inspiration for several other similar games, and was played by countless kids in high school IT labs back in the day.

title: Duke Nukem
description: One of my all-time favorite action platformers. It just has excellent level design, items, enemies, and interactivity. This is the first appearance of Duke Nukem, who would go on to further fame in his 3D series of games. In the original game he has a little less attitude but the outline of the character he would become is definitely here. The graphics look good (for EGA, that is). (Fun fact: Many of the game's sprites were directly ripped off from other games.) And even though the sounds are played through the PC speaker, they aren't that annoying! Overall this is a tremendously fun game that's definitely worth the download! Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Duke Nukem 3D
description: Does blowing away pigcops, destroying entire buildings, and shooting your way through an adult XXX store sound enjoyable? Then you'll love Duke 3D. It uses the "Build" engine, which is still similar to the old Wolf3D engine in that there are no rooms on top of other rooms, but the Build engine includes many new features, like walls of different heights and angles, lighting effects, and a versatile scripting system. Lots of fun! The first of several games using Ken Silverman's versatile engine, Duke Nukem 3D gets a lot right and has just the right "feel", especially in the introductory shareware episode. You can tell that a lot of time and care went into this release. (Note: Several people have emailed me to comment that there ARE rooms-above-rooms in Duke3D. While the effect of rooms-above-rooms can be _simulated_ in Build, there are never really any rooms on top of other rooms in the game, and thus it's not truly 3D.) Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem 3D, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Duke Nukem II
description: Between the original, classic Duke and the kickass Duke Nukem 3D came the unheralded sequel, Duke II. (Which really would've been Duke 4, if you counted the "registered-only" episodes 2 and 3.) The main advantages of the sequel over the original are in the areas of its graphics (in-game graphics, besides the introduction and some cutscenes, are still EGA, but they look better) and sound (SB instead of the PC speaker). It looks and sounds great, and the game is a bit more linear and action-focused compared to the exploration-heavy original game. However, despite the cool new effects, it doesn't seem quite as fun as the original. (There is a great recreation of the Duke II game engine for Windows, Mac, and Linux called Rigel Engine which allows wide-screen play at 60fps and several other nice features, so if you're playing on those platforms try it out! It needs a copy of the game to work.) Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem 2, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Dungeons of Drakklor
description: Dungeons of Drakklor is an action adventure game with some unique elements. Although it may look like it could be an RPG, it's actually closer to a more intentionally designed puzzle-like version of Gauntlet. Also, it may appear at first that the game is using a graphics mode, but it's actually using textmode with a modified character set (similarly to how Megazeux works) and two characters for every "sprite". This gives the game a unique look. In terms of gameplay, you are able to shoot your enemies, and in some cases trap them for extra coins. You need coins to pass through gates, which may require 10 or 100 coins to pass through. You can also pick up and move a single pushable block. There are 11 levels in the game and each covers an area larger than the screen so the viewport will scroll as you explore.

title: Dynamo Draughts
description: Draughts (aka "Checkers") is a strategy-based board game for two players. The object is to collect all of your opponents' pieces by jumping over them. This computerized version contains playing options, including adjustable board sizes from tiny 4x4 up to larger-than-usual 10x10. It includes three built-in settings: USA Pool, International, and Spanish, although you can customize it yourself. Strangely there doesn't seem to be a two-player option, so you must play against the computer, and there are no difficulty settings. There are a lot of other things though, like records of all the moves, saving / loading a game, etc. It uses the "WINDOS" system to simulate a Windows-like look in DOS.

title: Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms
description: The Earthworm Jim games are gaming classics, most famous on the 16-bit consoles (SNES and Genesis) but the games were also available for computer platforms such as DOS, WIndows, and Mac. The verbosely titled "Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms" is a collection of both of the first two games in a single package. All of the great animation and sounds from the games are here, as well as the levels. Unlike many early PC ports, the Earthworm Jim games translated very well to PCs. Run and gun in this demo version that offers levels from both games. Run EJW1.EXE and EJW2.EXE to play the demos of the first and second games, respectively. Note: Due to a weird glitch in the browser-based version, you must complete the setup process before playing! But if you download and run the game from your own PC, you shouldn't have that issue.

title: EdChess
description: EdChess (later re-published as commercial software under the more generic and enthusiastic name Chess!) is a computer chess program in text-mode. It allows play of two human players, play against the CPU, or watching a CPU vs CPU match. The pieces are represented crudely with 3x3 or 3x2 ASCII boxes. You can change the ability of the CPU by modifying the "difficulty" (maximum thinking time for the computer) and "think ahead" (whether the CPU can be processing while you're making your move). You can also review the moves made by going forward or backward. Overall it's a fairly basic but competent chess program.

title: EGA Trek
description: EGA Trek is based heavily on very early computer space simulation games. (ie. the first computer game ever, Space War!, aka Computer Space). Since this is a non-licensed game, it never refers to it as "Star Trek", but you know what they were going for. It includes color graphics that although sparse do the job well. The objective is to eliminate other ships and "save the galaxy". This is a simulation/strategy game with not a lot of action, so it won't be for everyone, but it definitely is a classic PC game.

title: Elder Scrolls: Arena
description: This is not a demo! It's the full version of this classic RPG game! It has been released by its original developers, and this is great news for all computer RPG fans. Similar to the more modern versions including Daggerfall, Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim, this game has obviously worse graphics but some say its gameplay is still superior. It has a very open-ended and non-linear feel so if you enjoy that type of game, please do check out Elder Scrolls: Arena! Video ReviewVideo review of Elder Scrolls: Arena, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall
description: Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall is the second game in the Elder Scrolls series which later spawned the more recent Elder Scrolls games. It's a first-person view 3D RPG that was once called "best CRPG of the year" and "a flawed masterpiece" by Computer Games Magazine (link). Daggerfall is an open-world game fan's dream as it allows you to roam freely and do what you want in it's huge world. The world is said to be 62,394 square miles in size. For comparison, that is approximately 4000 times as large as Oblivion's world! (See this map, with Daggerfall's size listed on the side.) It's quite amazing a world so large was packed into a file so relatively small (149 megs). The full version of this game was released for free by its owner. Video ReviewVideo review of Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Eliminator
description: Eliminator is a Snake / Nibbles / Tron lightcycles clone. Your job is to survive and avoid crashing into walls while your snake gets longer, as your opponent attempts to do the same. This game provides a two-player mode as well as a single player mode against a quite difficult computer opponent. CGA graphics are used and no sound effects. There are no options beyond the aforementioned settings besides setting the speed, but on modern computers you'll need to turn the speed way down to make this game playable.

title: Emerald Hunt
description: Emerald Hunt is a Boulderdash-inspired puzzle/strategy game with randomized levels. The goal of course is to collect as many emeralds as possible. Your bulldozer can plow through the dirt to reach them, however watch out for falling boulders that can crush you, and enemies that can kill you. The randomized levels mean that each time you play is different, although since the game is very simple each game will quickly start to feel similar since the different objects are literally strewn randomly around the map. The map is quite large and there are a lot of emeralds to collect, so finishing even one level will be a challenge.

title: Enchantasy: Quest For The Eternal Grimoire
description: Enchantasy seems to be a decent CRPG fantasy game, with the caveat that the author(s) REALLY want you to register this game. The story and environment seem pretty standard for this sort of game, with typical fantasy tropes. You walk around and use hotkeys to perform actions; thankfully the hotkeys are displayed on-screen at all times for easy reference. In the shareware version you are limited to saving your game 5 times. You can gain an additional 25 saves by noting the number the game provides when you go to save, visiting this archived page, and clicking on the number to get a 5-digit code for another 25 saves. Unfortunately the registered version seems to be unpreserved so all we'll get is the shareware game; use those saves wisely!

title: Epic Pinball
description: My favorite computer pinball games! The shareware version only contains one table, but it's really cool. Great graphics, smooth scrolling, SB sounds, and "good enough" physics. The screen scrolls to follow the ball, and while it's unfortunate that you never get to see the entire table at once, it allows for more detail to be shown on the screen. The shareware version includes a single table, Android (in later versions "Super Android"). It's really fun to play, and remember that a computer pinball game can do stuff you never could with a physical table. Ordering the whole collection from Epic (or more likely today, finding a digital copy online) would be worth it. Video ReviewVideo review of Epic Pinball, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Excelsior Phase One: Lysandia
description: Excelsior is an innovative and in-depth RPG. It uses text-mode graphics with a custom character set, 2x1 tiles (your character and most objects are two characters wide) and even includes animated tiles. The story involves being a "Fixer" who travels between dimensions solving irregularities / problems as they occur. It plays like a typical old-style RPG, with turn-based battles, many items / weapons / armors / spells to acquire, and a huge world to explore. You create your character before starting the game, choosing their name, stats, and initial skills. This is a great game for RPG fans. The is a more modern Windows version of the game available on the company's website, where you can still buy the full version of their games. Video ReviewVideo review of Excelsior Phase One: Lysandia, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Extreme Pinball
description: If you enjoyed Epic Pinball, you will also likely enjoy and appreciate Extreme Pinball, which uses the same engine. Released approximately two years after their earlier (and more well-known) games, Extreme Pinball was also released for the Sony Playstation. In this demo version, you get the "Rock Fantasy" table, which is one of the four tables included in the full version of the game. The action is fast-paced (perhaps slightly too fast at times) but I guess that's what makes it EXTREME! (The 90's were all about extreme-ness.) Generally good graphics and a rockin soundtrack make this a fun pinball game to play, even if the physics aren't the most accurate.

title: FaceTrex
description: FaceTrex is a block-sliding puzzle game which plays quite similarly to Soleau's earlier game Alpha Man. Again here you are pushing sliding blocks, but rather than spelling a word, you just need to get the "face blocks" onto their matching "face tiles". You'll need to carefully plan your moves so that none of your blocks get trapped. Thankfully you have unlimited retries and the levels can be restarted instantly. The game comes with a total of 25 levels for you to try; the first levels aren't too tough but, like many Soleau games, as you progress the levels get rather difficult! (At least, for me they are!)

title: Fairy Godmom
description: This is definitely a unique puzzle game. In it you play a fairy godmother ("Woah, couldn't have figured that out on my own", you say) who must collect magic coins on each board while avoiding killer crabs. (!?!) Anywho, the idea is to use your magic wand to "copy" objects and create them elsewhere to allow you to progress. (It makes sense when you actually play the game. Well, not the evil crabs stuff, but the magic wand stuff.) Neat game. (It used to be listed here as "Fairy Godmother" but that full title isn't used in the game itself.)

title: Fatal Fumes
description: Fatal Fumes is a top-down racing game in the style of Micro Machines racing games, and numerous others such as Super Speed or Slicks 'N Slide. The shareware version of this game offers four tracks to race, against the clock or against multiple CPU opponents. (The full version allows competition for two players simultaneously.) Tracks contain a bunch of different obstacles, like jumps, bridges, oil slicks, holes, etc. The game looks good and plays decently enough, although the controls are difficult to get used to; your car moves too fast and/or turns too slowly, at least that's how I experienced it

title: Final Impact
description: Final Impact is a game that possesses most of the qualities necessary for a hit game, with great production values, sound effects, and slick design. However, it unfortunately falls a bit short in the gameplay department. It's a mission-based shooting game with a similar format to Raptor, where you fly missions and earn money to buy new weapons and upgrades. The actual missions seem VERY difficult, and the way your ship fires (depending on the weapon, you can fire in 4 or 8 directions) is not easy to do. The default controls also probably will need to be reconfigured but thankfully you can do that within the game. Seems like a bit more playtesting would have made this game great, but as-is this demo is a great example of the kind of production values of this period of time. (Full game was released on CD with a full soundtrack.)

title: Football Fanatic
description: Quite different from modern football games, Football Fanatic is a sports management simulation game. That means it's all text (no graphics) and you don't actually play football, you manage the team's decisions, like financing, sponsorships, scouting, etc. This game won't be fun for a lot of people but there is still a niche market for games like this, so if you enjoy text-based sports sim games try this one out.

title: fRaBs
description: Abuse was a great side-scrolling action game that uses a unique system to control your character. You use the keyboard to move around and the mouse to aim your gun. It works pretty well and the game can be great fun to play, since it has nicely done graphics and sound effects, as well as many non-linear levels and powerups. This version of the game is also known as "Free Abuse", which is a fan project using the same engine (which was open-sourced by the devs) but including new levels and artwork. The original version of the game from Crack Dot Com is also available: Abuse

title: Fracas
description: Fracas is a well done Bomberman clone that has been given a fantasy themed makeover. In this game you play a wizard who lays magical "bombs" to defeat your enemies. Up to four players can play at once (sharing the same computer) and the game features nice smooth scrolling graphics and great sounds. (Note that this game was originally shareware but was recently released as freeware by its authors!)

title: Freaks!
description: Freaks! is an interesting 3D-ish FPS game from the mid 90's. Released in 1994 (after the original Doom) Freaks! is a decent looking game with a weird mechanic: Your character moves forward and backward smoothly, but when turning, you turn instantly at 90 degree angles, making the game feel somewhere between a FPS and a turn-based first-person RPG. You shoot at enemies and hit them if they are directly in front of you. So it's gameplay is more basic than even Wolfenstein 3D. There is only a single weapon, and you don't collect any items or powerups as far as I know. It's a shame because it has some pretty great art, although a little bit gruesome for kids! The original author(s) made a new version available (along with the source code) which runs in Windows natively and has actual FPS turning, so check that out here: Freaks 2.x Windows Port

title: Freddy Pharkas: Frontier Pharmacist
description: Freddy Pharkas: Frontier Pharmacist is one of the games that Al Lowe was the primary writer for during his time at Sierra. Besides of course the Leisure Suit Larry series. This demo version of the full graphic adventure game highlights the mouse-driven interface of the later Sierra titles, shared by other games of the time such as Space Quest IV. This game takes place during the gold rush era, and as usual you click around, die frequently, and eventually give up and use a hint guide. Sierra didn't produce many playable demos for their games; not sure why this one was chosen! But from what I've read it's an enjoyable game with rather obscure and inane puzzles that will perhaps have you reaching for that hint guide sooner than other games. (Note: I wasn't able to get the sound working in DOSBox, so I chose PC speaker in the setup program. Run SETUP.EXE and try your luck if you want working SoundBlaster or other sounds; you may need to play with DOSBox's options to get it working.)

title: Funballs
description: An innovative puzzle game where you attempt to match a pattern of balls that is shown on the right side of the screen. It's difficult to explain, but simple to learn to play. A nice, relaxing, challenging game.

title: G-Quest
description: G-Quest is a puzzle game where the object is to collect all of the gems, and push all of the "packages" into the "disposal units" in Sokoban-like fashion, in order to complete each level. There is no story, and your player is depicted as a generic ball. The levels are fairly large and varied, with many different obstacles that you will encounter. Since the levels and the sprites themselves are large, the levels scroll, which I found to be a bit disoriented due to the way that the scrolling occurs. There are a bunch of levels included, I'm not sure how many, but the registered "deluxe" version includes 50, so I imagine it's significantly less than that.

title: Galacta: The Battle for Saturn
description: Galacta: The Battle for Saturn (the game's full name) is a well-done remake of the Galaga or Galaxian type space shooting games. Your goal of course is to shoot down all of the enemies. Graphics are smooth and do the job nicely, but aren't that impressive. The gameplay is fast paced and the high challenge level will keep fans of the space shooting genre interested, with each wave being shorter but more active/intense than in the Galaga/Galaxian games.

title: Game Builder Lite
description: A system that supposedly allows you to create your own Sierra-like adventure game. However, although it features EGA graphics, walk-behinds, etc. I found the system to be limiting in many ways (besides the fact that it allows you to create only adventure games) and that it wasn't easy or intuitive to use. Check it out, but be wary ... AGS (Adventure Game Studio) is probably a more robust and overall better choice. (Note that this download is now actually for the full version, Game Builder Pro, which was released for free by MVP Software.)

title: Gobliiins
description: This demo version of the full game provides a brief glimpse into the humorous and entertaining adventure game Gobliiins, the first of a series of games. In the game you control three goblins (gobliiins?) each with a unique ability. In order to solve the puzzles, you will need to experiment and use each of their abilities: One uses items, another has great strength (punches things), and the third uses magic. The graphics and animation are great here (the memorable intro cutscene sets the tone), as are the sound effects, although there is no music. Great fun to play, although this demo version is limited, it gives you a glimpse into what you can expect in the full game.

title: Gobliins 2: The Prince Buffoon
description: Gobliins 2 is the sequel to the original Gobliiins adventure game. Like the first game, you control multiple goblins, but here there are only two: Fingus and Winkle. Both can pick up and use objects; the difference between them is in their personalities (Fingus=nice, Winkle=not) and how they react to what they encounter. The health bar is also gone, so the gameplay is simplified a bit, which could lead to less frustration in the puzzles. It's a very well put together game, using the same compelling aesthetic as the first. (This demo version contains the first four screens of the full game.)

title: Goldhunt
description: In this rare action/puzzle game by William Soleau (it's not listed on the Soleau Software website) the goal is to collect gold while pushing around blocks to trap enemies, or at least preventing their line of sight from seeing you. The trapping element is similar to the very old ASCII game Beast. There are different layouts, new enemies, and more intense challenges awaiting you as you progress through the levels. Your progress is shown on a map-like screen but it doesn't seem to serve any purpose since you simply go from one level to the next; there is no story. Graphics are usual 16-colors Soleau style.

title: Grand Theft Auto
description: Grand Theft Auto was certainly a unique and controversial game when it was released. In the game you play the role of a mob henchmen who must do various tasks like stealing cars, making deliveries or putting out a "hit" on someone. This version of the game (the original DOS demo version) features great sound and graphics (for the time it was released) and contains a good deal of gameplay from the full game. Needless to say this game is not intended for children and should not be downloaded by anyone under the age of 18 without permission from their parents!

title: GroundFire
description: GroundFire is a pretty basic shooting game, where you control a tank of some sort that moves along the bottom of the screen. Helicopters fly by, and you try to shoot at them while avoiding their missiles. Sometimes some powerups drop. There are sound effects that play as you battle, but they are pretty underwhelming. The game also gets choppy with a cycle count that is too high; I've set it here at 3000 which seems a bit slow, but higher than that and the game gets difficult to play. This one has relatively high production values for a self-produced game but more work was needed on the core gameplay.

title: Guimo
description: Guimo is an impressive looking game which seems to have a lot of promise, but the actual gameplay is a bit lacking. In this game, your character has to blast through the levels in a style similar to later Apogee platformers like Alien Carnage and perhaps most directly to Epic's Jazz Jackrabbit, and you can pick up a variety of weapons to do it. The main downfall of this game is its level design, which is difficult to navigate, as well as the enemies which seem to target you and attack you mercilessly even from far away in the level.

title: Hamster Republic Role Playing Game Construction Engine
description: Although I have little experience with this strangely named game creation system, the end results of this program can be quite impressive. This is a game creation system taylored specifically to the creation of role playing games. It does not seem to be a very easy program to learn to use properly, so be sure to make use of resources available on the official website. Recent versions of the source code are available under the GPL. All newer versions of this software are released in Windows and Linux versions only, though the original DOS version will remain available. If you're looking to build a new game using this engine, you should probably use a recent Windows version.

title: Hang!man
description: Well ... it's hangman, and it's a pretty basic implementation of the classic game normally played with a pen and paper by people who are very bored and have few entertainment options available to them. The game includes a fairly large word list; however, most of the words are short and uninteresting (like 'cool' or 'start'). The word list can be customized, though. The graphics are also pretty poor, and there's no sounds ... but hey, how much do you want from a game that only takes up 72k of disk space?

title: HangMan!
description: HangMan! (or "Larry's Hangman") is a decent Hangman game that plays just like the popular pen-and-paper word-guessing game. It comes with a bunch of different word lists, and you can add your own words as well. There are some options to set before starting a game which can affect the difficulty. Overall it's a decent version of the classic game. It's only one player though so if you want to play with a friend, get out the paper & pencil!

title: Hank's Quest: Victim of Society
description: Hank's Quest: Victim of Society is described by the authors as being "A whole new adventure-game in that 'Classic Sierra Style' we all came to love so dearly". Well since it seems to use the actual Sierra AGI engine, it should resemble the old Sierra adventures quite strongly! Your quest in this game as the titular Hank is to host a party at your parents' house. You begin the game without much direction and need to figure out what to do and where to go. The graphics are in the same style as the authentic Sierra games and look quite good. The music is apparently ripped from other games (it's credited to Al Lowe). Generally seems like a fun time if you like the early graphical adventure games.

title: Happyland Adventures
description: With nice looking graphics and fun sound effects/music, this game is quite enjoyable to play. The object is to collect happyland residents (little monster-guys). After you've collected and dropped off all of them (in the "happyzone"), you can exit the level. There are also many secret locations to find, and a level-editor is included to make your own levels! A polished platforming game which uses sprites from the free SpriteLib library by Ari Feldman.

title: Happyland Adventures: X-mas Edition
description: This version of Happyland Adventures includes more of the platforming and collecting action that the original game provides, with a whole set of new winter / holiday themed levels. In fact this package includes both the Xmas levels and the original levels, as well as the map editor (Windows only) to create your own levels and play them. Just like the original version, in the Xmas Edition, the object is to collect happyland residents (little monster-guys). After you've collected and dropped off all of them (in the "happyzone"), you can exit the level. Happy graphics (thanks to the free SpriteLib library of free sprites by Ari Feldman) and happy sounds round out this solid package.

title: Helious 2
description: Helious II is the sequel to the original blue ball filled with air that's slowly deflating game. Originally this game was only available when you registered the first game, but the developer has released it for free. This game includes many more action/puzzle levels which will test your dexterity as you try to zip through as quickly as possible without crashing into the walls. The graphics and overall design are the same as the first game; this game just adds more levels. Still a fun and unique game to play.

title: Heretic
description: Based on the DOOM engine, Heretic was only mildly popular on its release because there were so many copycat 3D-shooting games released around the same time. However, Heretic is one of the better shooting games released in the pre-Quake era. It has solid level design, good graphics & sounds (although of course you're limited to 320x200) and really the only major criticism that could be leveled at it is that it's too much like DOOM. Video ReviewVideo review of Heretic, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Hero's Heart
description: Hero's Heart is a traditional pushing, block moving puzzle game (think Boxxle, or even Chip's Challenge). The object varies from level to level, but usually consists of collecting all of the hearts on the level and getting to the green exit. There are lots of similar games out there (graphics are minimalist, sound is nonexistent) but if you enjoy this type of game, get ready for lots of difficult puzzles.

title: Heroes
description: This game is great! In it, your task is to drive your snake around and try to force the other snakes to crash into you (or the walls). Yes, it sounds like the classic "Nibbles" type game, but this game offers much more ... like great VGA graphics and sounds, many different gameplay modes, power-up items, multiplayer play, and lots more! A must download. (Note that it can be a bit too violent for younger players.)

title: Hexen: Beyond Heretic
description: The sequel to the popular Heretic game, Hexen takes the Heretic engine and adds some notable improvements, like weather effects, breakable environments, roleplaying elements and less linear gameplay. Instead of just playing through levels, you must venture through the "hub" which connects various worlds. The atmosphere created in this game is well done, and if you're a fan of early 3D shooting games chances are you'll enjoy this 4-level DEMO version of Hexen.

title: Hexxagon
description: An extremely enjoyable puzzle game. It's quite similar to Reversi/Othello, except with a hexagon grid rather than a square grid. The object is to take over the gameboard (which can be edited by the user and saved) with marbles (gems?) of your own color. It includes a single player vs. computer option (with three skill levels) and also a two player option. Definitely fun to play, as it's got a really nice looking interface, and, on the 'easy' setting, I can sometimes actually win! :)

title: Highway Hunter
description: Highway Hunter is a vertical shooting game with great production values (animated cut-scenes, well-drawn SVGA graphics, parallax scrolling, great music) and intense action. In the game, you must drive along the futuristic roads and blast everything in your path. You will of course collect powerups to upgrade your weapons, and improved shields to protect your car. The fact that this game takes place on highway roads rather than in space means that your movement is a bit more restricted, and it makes the game stand out a bit more from other shmups. It's generally a top-notch shoot-em-up and shooting fans will definitely want to give it a try! Video ReviewVideo review of Highway Hunter, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Hocus Pocus
description: Simply a great platform game. Similar to Clyde's Adventure and Clyde's Revenge (also developed by Moonlite Software) but Hocus Pocus has better graphics, plus it's more exciting because there are enemies to kill! Here you play a wizard who runs around the levels shooting enemies and triggering switches and walls. The pace of the game (like the Clyde series) is more laid back than frantic; if you're careful and methodical, you'll do well. (The FILE_ID.DIZ description compares to to the Super Mario Bros series, but it's really not too similar.) If you haven't played Hocus Pocus, you definitely should. Video ReviewVideo review of Hocus Pocus, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Hopy-ONE
description: Hopy-ONE (or in some places at least, "Cyborg Hopy-ONE") is a strange single-screen platformer game. You control your robot, which has unique ways of moving around the screen. It has an awkward jump, and also these tendrils that you can extend to keep you in the air and then move around horizontally. It's about as awkward as it sounds when I try to describe it. On each level you must collect all the orbs then make it to the exit, or one of multiple exits. Graphics are decent but sounds effects are repetitive and get old fast. Definitely unique but not something I would personally want to play.

title: Hubie
description: Hubie is not a well known game, but it probably should be. The game (slickly presented with smooth animations and sound effects) involves action, platforming and puzzle elements. The goal is to get Hubie to the exit of the level. Hubie has many abilities, such as pushing objects, crushing breakable objects, "coptering", blowing and climbing. There's a good variety to the various levels but since Hubie has so many different abilities, the initial learning curve is high.

title: Hugo III: Jungle of Doom
description: The third and last game in the Hugo series which began with the much more widely-known Hugo's House of Horrors. This game takes place after a plane crash in the jungle, after which Penelope is bitten by a poisonous snake. It's again up to Hugo to save the day! The same game engine is used as the previous games, with a few tweaks, like a hints engine. Hugo's sprite will also change size as he moves farther into the background. The EGA graphics are generally quite good as this game brings the series to a close. It's safe to say that if you enjoyed the first two games, you'll likely enjoy the finale as well!

title: Hugo's House of Horrors
description: This game is the first in the Hugo trilogy of graphical adventure games. Done in the style of those classic Sierra adventures, these feature EGA graphics and annoying PC speaker effects (which, thankfully, can be easily turned off). They're all fun to play, though, especially if you enjoy graphic adventure games. This first game introduces the characters, and while it's a bit short (it can be finished very quickly if you know what you're doing) that doesn't mean that it's easy! The game has a "horror" vibe but there's nothing too scary about it. Good for playing on Halloween? Video ReviewVideo review of Hugo's House of Horrors, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Humbug
description: Humbug is one of the rare text adventure games you'll find on DOSGames.com, and it's here because it is truly a classic of the text adventure genre. The game has a Christmas theme. There are tons of locations to explore in this lengthy and well written adventure game, which contains over 200 objects. The author, Graham Cluely, has since become a well-known computer security expert, but back at this time

title: Indiana Jones and the Fate Of Atlantis
description: This demo version of the interactive Indiana Jones adventure game gives you an idea what to expect in the full game (if you can find it, that is ...) Made by LucasArts, this game shares both the great LucasArts interface and great production values. The game involves Indy investigating the lost "City of Atlantis" (duh). Overall this demo looks and sounds quite impressive, and the well thought out interface makes it easy to get into. (I am not sure how long this demo is because I didn't complete it, so don't be too surprised/disappointed when it ends!)

title: Inner Worlds
description: An enchanting fantasy-themed platform game that few have likely heard of, Inner Worlds features great graphics, sound, music, variety and game mechanics. The protagonist in the game may remind you a bit of Jill of the Jungle, but the gameplay here is more in-depth, with various items to pickup and use. Your character can also change forms, from a woman to a wolf. Very impressive game! The authors have given permission to distribute the registered version, so this is the full version of this game! However if you would like to support the original developers, you can buy a copy on Steam here! Video ReviewVideo review of Inner Worlds, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Interpose
description: Interpose is a well designed horizontal shooting game with good graphics and sound effects. There's not much story, but as you fly your ship through the various levels you will shoot down a variety of enemies while collecting powerups as well as money, which can be exchanged for ship upgrades in stores. You can also save your progress to load later, which is rare feature in shoot-em-up games. Overall it's a very professionally done game which is worth checking out for fans of the genre.

title: Interpose Xmas Greetings
description: Interpose X-mas Greetings is a special Christmas-themed demo of the full Interpose space shoot-em-up game. It features merry holiday themed levels where you happily shoot reindeer and other Christmasy things. What better way to celebrate the holidays? But it's okay because these aren't the REAL Santa & reindeers, they are merely constructions of an evil scientist! Okay, anyways, since it maintains the same gameplay and production values as the actual Interpose game it plays pretty well and looks nice.

title: Invasion of the Mutant Space Bats of Doom
description: Nice name, eh? It certainly caught your attention! This space shooting game has pretty VGA graphics and smooth gameplay. It's got a variety of 'space bats' to kill and different ship powerups as well, somewhat in the same style as the Galaga and other games of that style (waves of enemies). Pretty good sound effects, too. Though maybe better known for the name than for anything else. (Note: I occasionally had some problems when using the keyboard in the game, although when I switched and used the mouse, I had no problems.)

title: Iron Blood
description: Iron Blood (aka Interrupt in Korea) is a professionally produced platforming game (say that three times fast) released in 1996. First you choose one of two mechs: The red mech is slower but more powerful with a rocket booster, while the blue mech is faster but weaker. Then you progress through the stages from left to right, with some exploration but still mostly linearly. The graphics and sounds are well done and fit the game well, with nice animations on your mech, which is a large sprite. The levels (of which only one of the total six is available in the demo version) are not particularly interesting or well designed which is probably the most significant issue with the game.

title: Isle Wars
description: In this strategy style game your goal is to take over the world! It's similar to the classic game Risk, but adds some new elements like natural disasters. There's quite a lot of thinking and planning required to be sucessfull. You play against computer opponents ... luckily you can adjust the difficulty level! There is no multiplayer in this game even though it may seem like a natural fit. It may not have the greatest graphics or sound effects but it's definitely enjoyable if you like this sort of game.

title: Iter Vehemens ad Necem
description: Iter Vehemens ad Necem (aka IVAN) means, in Latin, "Violent Road to Death". It is a Roguelike with graphics, and although rarely mentioned alongside other more well-known Roguelike examples, it seems to have a lot of polish and features. Like others in the genre, each world that you explore is unique. There are towns, dungeons, and many places to explore and, probably, die horribly. There are also a lot of keyboard commands to memorize, but you can always press ? to view a list of them. Overall it seems to have plenty of features and decent graphics (in 800x600 resolution!) as well. There is even an unofficial effort to continue developing the game (on non-DOS platforms) over at attnam.com so check that out if you're a fan of the game, there is tons of information available there.

title: Jack in the Dark
description: Jack in the Dark was a promotional game given out in the Christmas 1993 season to promote the release of Alone in the Dark 2. It's a short adventure game using the typical Alone in the Dark engine so if you love the particular look of the original AITD game you'll enjoy the aesthetics of this adventure. The plot involves a tricker-treating kid who gets trapped in a bizarre and eerie toy store on Halloween. Fun to play albeit rather short, it was a free promo game after all.

title: Jason Jupiter, Star Cadet, In 'Unfinished Business'
description: Unlike the first game in the Jason Jupiter series, which is a platformer, this sequel is a Boulderdash-like game. The object is to collect the required number of borxidium (heart-shaped symbols) and then make it to the exit, while avoiding monsters and falling rocks. There are actual graphics this time (CGA sprites) instead of the text-mode characters used in the first game. Levels span multiple screens, and unlike the first game, you don't need to collect EVERY heart to progress, only the required number displayed at the bottom of the screen. It also includes an editor to edit the game's levels!

title: Jazz Jackrabbit
description: A pretty cool platform game that tries to borrow from Sonic the Hedgehog, with mixed results. It actually plays a bit slower than Sonic, but includes more shooting action. Basically you (Jazz Jackrabbit) run through nice-looking VGA levels, collecting upgrades to your guns, while blasting mostly cute enemies. And of course watching out for carrots. Fun, but the levels get a bit repetitive at times. (Fun fact: Cliff Bleszinski (of Unreal and Gears of War fame) was one of the designers of this game.) Video ReviewVideo review of Jazz Jackrabbit, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Jazz Jackrabbit: Holiday Hare 1994
description: This special freeware version of the classic Sonic-inspired jumping & shooting game from Epic Megagames was released at Christmas time in 1994 to promote the full version of Epic's Jazz Jackrabbit series. The Jazz games of course combine the fast speed of the Sonic games along with shooting action. This "Holiday Hare" version includes the great graphics, smooth animation, wonderful music and excellent controls of the other Jazz games, along with a winter/holiday theme and some bonus "3D" gem collecting stages.

title: Jetpack
description: This game is great! It's a platform game where you jump or fly around the various boards using your jetpack, collecting items and avoiding monsters. Collect all of the gems and then exit the level; don't forget to pick up fuel to keep your jetpack powered up. It's got tight controls, enjoyable graphics, and funny sound effects. Best of all, it includes an editor, with which you can create and save your own levels! (Jetpack 2 was recently released by Adept Software, almost 20 years after the original game!) Video ReviewVideo review of Jetpack, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Jetpack Christmas Special
description: This special promotional freeware version of the excellent Jetpack game was released in 1993 to promote Software Creations' full-version Jetpack game and their other software. It features some Christmas themed graphics: You play as Santa and collect presents, among other graphical flourishes. Otherwise it's very similar to the original Jetpack game, with an included level editor, etc. (Jetpack 2 was recently released by Adept Software, almost 20 years after the original game!)

title: Jill of the Jungle
description: This is the first game released by Epic after the famous ZZT series. It's still pretty cool, too. You play as Jill of the Jungle, and jump around in various VGA-styled levels, collecting apples and battling strangely designed creatures in a memorable jungle-ish world. A good mix of action and adventure, along with a couple little (fairly easy) puzzle sections. Although the controls take some getting used to, this game is worth playing. Jill ended up being one of the more well-known shareware game characters. Get the full version for free from GOG.com! Video ReviewVideo review of Jill of the Jungle, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Joust VGA
description: Joust VGA is a clone of the famous Joust arcade game, which many other later games took as inspiration. (Perhaps most notably Balloon Fight on the NES.) The object is to ride your flying ostrich around the screen and joust the other riders off of their ostriches. The game plays quite well (although you may need to adjust the speed to avoid it playing super-fast) even though only the one-player mode is included in the shareware version. The graphics are faithful to the original and the game has a satisfying feel as you flap around and try to unseat the other riders.

title: Jungle Jack
description: Jungle Jack is a Pipe Dream / Pipe Mania clone where the objective is to make a path for the water to travel to its intended target(s). You begin with a series of paths at the bottom of the screen, and you need to place them in order to make a smooth path for the water. On subsequent placements, you're only given two paths to choose from. You've only got 60 seconds to finish your path before the water starts so don't dawdle too long! Unlike some of Soleau's other early games this one features actual graphics.

title: Kaboom
description: Kaboom is not a variant of the classic Atari 2600 game Kaboom. (If you're looking for that, try Kerboom! which is a decent DOS clone.) Anyways, this game is a deathmatch fighting game for up to four players. At least two human combatants are required, otherwise it'll be rather boring since there are no CPU opponents available. (This is apparently a public beta version so it's missing some features the author planned for the full game.) There are no weapons other than the default blaster, so you'll need to use that (and avoid all of the other things trying to kill you) to take out your opponents as you fly around the gritty industrial type arenas. It looks good and controls well, and there are plenty of options to tinker with, but the core gameplay won't likely hold your attention for too long, especially if you don't have a second player around to play with.

title: KBall
description: KBall is a beautifully designed ball-rolling game ala Marble Madness, but probably less stress-inducing than that classic game. It was originally released in 2003 but the DOS port was just made available in 2020. The goal is to collect all of the orbs then roll your ball to the exit. You'll need to be careful not to fall off the platform and move fast, because the timer is quickly ticking down. The game features great high-res graphics and several different level packs to try, including both easy beginner levels and challenging levels to frustrate even experienced players.

title: KKND: Krush Kill 'N Destroy
description: KKND is a real-time strategy game (RTS) with a futuristic, post-apocalyptic theme, pitting humans against mutants. The two sides fight against each-other with a variety of different units, which you direct in real-time. In the full game, each faction has its own separate campaign of 15 missions, but here in the demo you get a single mission to play. I am not too knowledgeable about this genre but based on the review scores this game got on launch it's pretty good so you should check it out.

title: Klass of 99
description: Klass of 99 is a remake / update of a classic ZX Spectrum Skool Daze and Back To Skool games from the 1980's. You play as Eric, a troublemaker who is on a quest to delete his permanent record from his school's computer. In order to do so, you'll need to help him get onto the headmaster's computer without getting caught too many times by the teachers. The graphics and sounds have received significant upgrades from the original, and the pixel art is well drawn and quite charming. The game controls well, although the multiple different buttons are hard to remember. Also if you've never played the original you'll likely have no idea what to do at first; see the beginner's help guide for some tips to get you started!

title: Kosmonaut
description: Kosmonaut is in some ways the prototype of a more advanced game, Skyroads. The title screen even seems to say "Skyroads" in an elaborate font. The concept is a 3D "racing" game where the only goal is to reach the end of the course. You do so by controlling your speed and jumping at the right moments. The game is tough, mainly because when you crash or fall off the track, it mocks you and then you have to start over! But it's an interesting first concept that was developed more fully in later games. (We can also see how this game influenced modern games, such as Snail Mail for iPhone/iPad.)

title: Krypton Egg
description: Like Arkanoid ... except better! Described as "the ultimate Breakout", this Arkanoid "clone" isn't really a clone at all. It features great graphics, cool sounds, and varied level design. The best part, however, are the cool powerups that drop down. In some levels, the screen gets really crazy with all of the balls and powerups and enemies flying around. The only major complaint is that the ball bounces the same regardless of where it hits your paddle. This game was, many years later, remade as an app for modern mobile devices.

title: Ladder Man
description: Ladder Man is the first in a series of side-view puzzle games by Soleau Software. (The third game is available here: Ladder Man III. It seems like the second game was only available if you registered the first game.) Anyways this is a puzzle game where the object is to use your ladder, and push around various blocks, to collect all the diamonds and avoid anything that will kill you. Much like real life: Collect $, avoid dying. There are a variety of levels to choose from, and a visual tutorial that walks you through how the game works. The visuals are better in the sequel, but there is still plenty of content here for puzzle fans.

title: Lemmings
description: Most people have probably played (or at least seen) some version of the classic Lemmings game designed by DMA Design. The object is to guide your "Lemmings" (actually little green-haired guys) to the level exit. To do so you assign your Lemmings jobs, like digger, or bridge-builder, to guide them past the various obstacles. A classic puzzle game that can sometimes also require quick reflexes! :) (This is the demo version of the game; unfortunately it crashes in the in-browser version of DOSBox we're using so you'll need to download it and run it locally to play it.) Video ReviewVideo review of Lemmings, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Lure of the Temptress
description: The first game ever published by Revolution Games, it was recently made available for free download for the first time! In this graphical adventure game you play the role of Diermot, who starts the game in a prison cell. The game has decent graphics and sound effects, and is generally quite fun to play. The only complaint about it is that is is rather short, but it is still quite enjoyable to play. (Note from the game's authors: "When the game first begins, move the cursor to the menu at the top of the screen and RESTART the game. This bypasses the copy protection system.")

title: Mad Painter
description: Mad Painter is a Pac-Man type game that differentiates itself through its theme and the scrolling city in which you play. The goal is to paint lines on the streets, and the level ends when you cover all the streets. However there are of course "crazy cars" that will attempt to crash into you. There are no Pac-Man style power pellets, but you can press Spacebar to honk your horn and try to get the other cars to turn around! It's a near little game that seems to use text mode with an edited character set for the actual game portion, but uses graphics mode for the title screen, menu, and endgame screens! Unfortunately you only get one life, so a single mistake ends your game and you have to start over.

title: Magic Carpet
description: Magic Carpet is a unique 3D experience. You play a mage who rides a magic carpet, and your goal in each level (50 in the full game, two in this demo) is to collect enough mana to fill your castle. You collect it via golden balls, and you'll also need to watch out for enemies such as giant worms and rival mages flying on their own carpets. The game is visually impressive and fluid, although with a short draw distance (lots of "fog"). This two-level demo gives you a taste of what the full game has to offer. Video ReviewVideo review of Magic Carpet, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Magus
description: Magus is a roleplaying game created by Ronny Wester, better known for his Cyberdogs and C-Dogs action games. This, however, is a somewhat small-scale and comical turn-based RPG. You begin by creating your party, which includes the usual character types (such as barbarian and wizard) and not-so common types (duck and duck wizard). Then you proceed to move each member of your party in turn around the map, collecting treasure and fighting enemies. It can be somewhat tedious to move each character, and there's really no plot. However, the graphics have an endearing quality to them, and there is some random humor in the game that helps keep things interesting.

title: Major Stryker
description: This is a great EGA shooting game from Apogee, who were better known for their platform games like Keen and the original Duke Nukem series. However this game is also pretty well made. It features frantic graphics and SoundBlaster sounds/music. There are lots of ship powerups and lots of enemies to fight. The only problem is that sometimes there is so much going on that it's hard to keep track of what is an enemy and what's part of the background. (3D Realms (formerly known as Apogee) released the full version of this game as freeware.) Video ReviewVideo review of Major Stryker, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Mario & Luigi
description: Mario & Luigi is a clone of the popular Super Mario Bros game for the NES. The game has an interesting backstory, where the developer Mike Wiering made the game as a programming exercise, and a beta version somehow leaked out and even was taken and sold by another guy! (You can download this alternate version in the "extra files" area above.) The actual game, titled Mario & Luigi later released by Wiering (obviously with no official license from the "Big N") offers decent gameplay and six levels to complete. The engine was obviously re-used for later games such as Charlie the Duck, Sint Nicolaas, and the most obvious being Super Angelo! Anywho, this game is generally fun to play, and the executable is only 57k! (The Turbo Pascal 6.0/5.5 source code is available on the Wiering Software website as well.)

title: Mario Bros VGA
description: A mostly faithful version of the original Mario Bros arcade game. Kick turtles! Hit the POW block! It's how many were introduced to Mario before his NES debut. This version includes VGA graphics (not very pretty graphics, though) as well as two player gameplay ... unfortunately two players is not offered in the shareware version, only in the registered full version. (The original game was of course made by Nintendo, who had nothing to do with this remake.)

title: Mario Teaches Typing
description: If you were a kid with a PC but no Super Nintendo Entertainment System back in 1992 (or even the original NES) it may have been exciting to hear that there were some official Mario games coming to PC! Unfortunately they were "edutainment" games created by Interplay, not by Nintendo themselves. Mario Teaches Typing is at least upfront about what it is. The game does LOOK like a Mario game with colorful graphics and well known characters like Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad making appearances. And it does attempt to teach you typing through a series of four typing mini games. This demo version seems to only include the first of these mini games, "Mario's Smash & Dash", whereas the full version also includes "Mario's Wet World Challenge", "Mario's Tunnel Of Doom", and "Mario's Expert Express", all of which are likely less fun than they sound. The program does seem to keep track of the player's statistics and allows for multiple profiles.

title: Math Rescue
description: This game is very similar to another Apogee game, Word Rescue, but with a math theme. Supposedly an educational game, this game doesn't seem to provide as much educational merit as some other titles, but it sure is fun for an "educational" game. It's from Apogee (publisher of many shareware classics like Commander Keen), so you know it'll have good control, graphics, etc. Its attempts to be educational can be annoying at times ... Basically you're trying to answer simple math questions while avoiding enemies. Video ReviewVideo review of Math Rescue, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Matrix
description: Matrix is a great Tetris variant which in most respects plays the same as the original game, but adds several options and variations, as well as presenting the game in a visually appealing yet still simple way. The basic gameplay is the same: Make lines by fitting falling pieces into the well. There are multiple speeds and handicaps to set, as well as "Scenarios" (which start with the well partially filled). You can record your playing session to watch again later, and you can also save your game and load it to continue at a later time. The controls work fluidly and since it offers many options it's a solid choice to play a game of Tetris!

title: Mechwar
description: Mechwar is a turn-based strategy game based on the world of FASA Battletech, which I know nothing about. I imagine it's a decent simulation / homage for those who understand the intricacies of mechs and all of the number-crunching involved. This game allows you to create your own mechs, and maps, and more, and play out scenarios in a turn-based mouse-controlled fashion. I don't have the attention span or interest to learn how to play, but I imagine if you're interested in this sort of game you probably already know quite a lot about it. It includes a helpful menu which allows you to choose from all of the various designers included

title: Megazeux
description: The best, most flexible game creation system created for MS-DOS, in my opinion. While it doesn't allow for the best graphics (it's in text mode, but you can edit the ASCII characters), it's extremely flexible, and it also allows Soundblaster music and sound effects. Games are created using a GUI to place various blocks, and programs are written using the built-in OOP Robotic programming language. There are also plenty of user created games available and there were also many webpages dedicated to it. Check it out. Video ReviewVideo review of Megazeux, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Menace of Dr Spoil Sport
description: Oh no! Dr Spoil Sport plans to destroy the Earth with his super laser on his floating space station! Only YOU can stop him by teleporting there and disabling this fiendish weapon! So in this "virtual reality" game (created using the Virtual Reality Studio software) you run (or slowly stumble your way through) a simulated 3D-ish environment and click on things to try to get to the next area. Like most Virtual Reality Studio engine games, it's a bit awkward to navigate around, and knowing what to do takes a lot of trial and error. There is some shooting, but the gameplay actually has more puzzle-solving and exploration than action. However there is an attempt here to do something interesting with the engine, so if you have the patience to battle the user interface you may enjoy this.

title: Meteor
description: The oddly named Meteor is a really great action/adventure game. As a soldier, you must complete various missions. There can be different objectives, but most end up being sorta like "kill all the guys dressed in red". (Your guy is dressed in green.) That's okay though because the game's graphics, sounds, and gameplay are all great! Lots of shooting/explosions, definitely a fun game for action fans. The game even includes an editor to create your own missions and lets you edit the graphics!

title: Mice Maze
description: Mice Maze is plays very similarly to the Crusher and Crusher's Castle 2 games, also by Soleau Software. So if you've played those, you know what to expect here, except this time it's about mice and cheese, and cats on the prowl trying to kill you. If you haven't played the Crusher games, Mice Maze is a randomly generated puzzle / action game where you must discover the location of your lost mouse friend. The good part about randomly generated rooms is that the game is different each time you play. The bad is that the design will be, well, random, so some rooms will be very easy and others will be nearly impossible. Still it's decently fun to play and continues the mice theme that other Soleau games share. (Mice Moves and Mice Men.)

title: Mice Men
description: Mice Men is an original and addicting puzzler, one of the many creations of Soleau Software. The object is to get all of your 'mice men' to the other side of the board. This is accomplished by pulling up or down on the columns to create paths for them to walk. Like most Soleau Software puzzle games, it's easy to learn, and fun to play, but tough to master. Sounds like the perfect puzzler, eh? Cute EGA mice graphics, too.

title: Micro Machines
description: Micro Machines received good reviews upon its original release, especially for the NES. The concept is that you are racing the tiny "Micro Machine" brand cars around typical locations like a table, where items like pencils and notebooks become huge obstacles on the race track. The PC version features fast and furious gameplay along with decent aesthetics. The action may be too frantic, actually, since it's difficult to control your car. I'm not exactly sure what speed the original game is supposed to run at, but at any speed, navigating the course is challenging, especially when the computer opponents don't seem to have any trouble with it!

title: Micro's Dilemma II
description: Micro's Dilemma II is the sequel to the original Micro game, however it was released several years before the Micro! Deluxe game. The gameplay is similar to the other games in the series, albeit with not as refined graphics, UI, and gameplay as the Deluxe version. The goal is still to cause the laser to pass through all of the spheres; you do so by aligning mirrors to reflect the laser as well as using any of the other objects on the playing field. There is some decent puzzle action here, although as mentioned the deluxe version above is probably a better choice.

title: Mimi & the Mites
description: Hidden gem alert! Mimi & the Mites is a well-made platforming game where you must kill the mites and get to the exit. To do so, you'll need to shoot 'em, avoid 'em, and use various environmental tools like elevators, teleporters, and trampolines. The game features high production values with great graphics and animations, as well as music and sound effects. The levels are tricky but not too difficult (at least not the early ones) so it's a fun game that everyone should try. (The release status of this one is a bit strange, the title screen clearly states this is freeware, but a later release is clearly shareware, so I'm not sure exactly what the deal is here.)

title: Mine Mayhem
description: Mine Mayhem is a great Minesweeper clone with many options which plays smoothly. In addition to the regular options you would find in Windows Minesweeper, Mine Mayhem also offers hexagonal shaped tiles, clear or "walk across" type gameplay, different levels of hint modes to help newer players, lots of statistics and high score tables, and a variety of configuration options to tweak the gameplay. Mouse support is of course included, and it controls the same as the familiar Windows version. Overall it's a great option for DOS Minesweeper and is highly recommended. Source code in C++ is also available.

title: Mirror Magic
description: Mirror Magic is a puzzle game involving lasers and mirrors. It is, according to the author, a clone of the Commodore 64 game "Deflektor" and was originally released for the Amiga as "Mindbender". It's also been released for Windows and other platforms, and in fact that version is more up-to-date than the older DOS version provided here. Anyways, in each level, you have to adjust the various parts on screen via mouse input to use your laser ("magic beam") to collect the "magic kettles". The game comes with a set of pre-made levels, and you can make your own in the level editor. While this is not the kind of game I personally enjoy, it's undeniable that it's well made, with nicely drawn graphics and sound effects / music. The source code is provided in the ZIP file.

title: Monkey Island, The Secret of
description: This demo version of the classic Secret of Monkey Island game (the first in the series) gives you a taste of why this series (and this game in particular) have become cult gaming classics. The excellent writing, memorable characters, exquisite art and of course numerous humorous situations really make this game stand out from other more mundane adventure games. Unfortunately it's only a demo but you can purchase the original or the updated HD remake online.

title: Monster Bash
description: This is another of Apogee's EGA sidescrollers. This one is lesser known because it was a bit outdated when it was released ... VGA graphics were quickly becoming the norm by that time. However, while it IS a bit more linear than their previous games, it's still worth a look if you enjoyed Apogee's other EGA platformers. In this game you play a kid ("Johnny Dash") who is trying to rescue captured animals, and to do it, he must use his trusty slingshot to kill various undead and ... uh, alive enemies. Spooky! There are three difficulty settings so you should be able to get far even if you're no good at games. Check out the Monster Bash HD remake on GOG.com for the new and improved modern remake of this game! Video ReviewVideo review of Monster Bash, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Moraff's World
description: Moraff's World is one of several first-person RPG dungeon crawling games released by Moraffware in the early 90's. There really is no story to consider, so the entirety of the game is exploring various dungeon and dungeon-like areas to kill monsters (over 40 different kinds) and collect items. Like other Moraff games you're presented with a plethora of different graphical options upon running the game but which one you select won't have much impact on the game itself. I found it somewhat disorienting having the four different views, but I suppose it helps to be able to see your surroundings. If you're a fan of first-person dungeon crawlers check it out, otherwise, there's not much here for you ...

title: Mortal Kombat 2
description: In terms of ports, DOS often received pretty terrible ones in the early days. (See for example Mega Man or Double Dragon for DOS ... or better yet, avoid them entirely.) However Mortal Kombat 2 is a surprisingly faithful rendition of the arcade classic game. Mortal Kombat is of course the supremely violent one-on-one fighting game series, famous for its Fatalities, violence, and unique combat system. This demo version only allows fights between Liu Kang and Reptile, however the full version features all 15 fighters. The graphics and sounds are relatively faithful to the arcade, and the game has the same feel, although of course using the keyboard to play will be nowhere near as satisfying as an arcade stick and buttons! (Note the keyboard controls below in the instructions.)

title: Mortal Kombat 3
description: This demo pre-release version of Mortal Kombat 3 allows you to play as either Jax or Sheeva in a 1-player vs computer, or 2-player match. This is of course the third in the long-running series of MK games, known for their violent fatalities and signature gameplay which fighting game fans often either love or hate. This third installment looks and feels very similar to the arcade game, which is no small feat on MS-DOS in 1995. Although only two characters are playable here, you can get a feel for the game, including the characters' special moves. The main limitation to playing it in DOS is using the keyboard to play, with the default keys (arrow keys plus the Insert-Del-PgUp-PgDn keys as your attack keys) being rather difficult to use. Modern solutions like Joy2Key can help make this game easier to play. The full version is available from GOG.com in a set with games 1 & 2 of the series for a reasonable price.

title: Mortar Mayhem
description: Mortar Mayhem is a copycat game, but a pretty good one. In Mortar Mayhem the object is to destroy your opponent's tanks by setting the angle and velocity of your shots. Gameplay is livened up a bit by the inclusion of various weapons that you can buy. The main quibble with this game is the lack of computer opponents; you can only play against other human players. Other that that it has good graphics, but Scorched Earth is still probably better in most aspects.

title: Ms Pacman PC
description: It's just like Pac-Man, but it's MS Pac-Man! What's the difference? Well, there's a bow on her ...This game IS a lot the same as the classic Pac-Man game, but with some variations, like different maze layouts and smarter ghosts. The graphics and sound effects attempt to imitate the original arcade game. It's an almost perfect conversion / remake, so if you liked the arcade, get this!

title: Need for Speed
description: The first game in the now venerable Need for Speed series made an appearance for DOS computers, in addition to the Playstation and other console platforms. This demo version of the game shows off its impressive 3D graphics (not assisted by special hardware) and sound effects ... impressive for 1995, anyways. It doesn't offer you any options but does allow you to race against computer controlled cars and get a feel for what the game is like. It does provide some simple but enjoyable racing action and serves as a prototype for future games in the series.

title: Nethack
description: Despite it's name, this game does NOT involve any type of computer "hacking". It's actually my favorite "Roguelike" game, orignally based on the "Hack" roguelike. While it may take awhile to learn all of the different commands, the game itself is very deep and involving. Plus, it's different each time you play. Unlike most Roguelikes, Nethack also features optional VGA graphics. This is one of the few games that I come back to play over and over, so I suggest you try it! (Check nethack.org for ports for Windows, Linux, and many more systems.)

title: Neut Tower
description: Neut Tower is a new MS-DOS game developed on actual 286 hardware and released for the DOS Games Jam. As such, although it is a new game, it very much has the feel of a puzzle game created back in the early 90's. The object is to escape the tower, with the aid of your AI entity; you can switch back and forth between the human protagonist and the AI at any time, and you'll need the abilities of both to get through all of the rooms. It plays well and looks good so give it a try and support the author if you like it! (Source code in C++ is included in the ZIP file.)

title: Nitemare 3D
description: From the creator of Hugo's House of Horrors comes this 3D shooter. (Previously misnamed on this website as "Nightmare 3D".) It's technical level is about the same as Wolfenstein 3D, but it DOES include some cool new stuff. The campy pseudo-horror motif is well done, and generally it's not entirely tedious to play, albeit unpolished and clearly an attempt to capitalize on the popularity of the then-new 3D shooter genre. Video ReviewVideo review of Nitemare 3D, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Nyet
