description: If you want a basic, no-frills Tetris game, this is probably it. It's old, but it plays well ... just don't expect any fancy graphics or features. It uses text mode (the same way that the original Tetris game coded by Alexey Pajitnov). The author claims it has "a more responsive feel" compared to the original game; you be the judge of that!

title: Offroad
description: Offroad is a Moon Patrol take-off which features smooth-scrolling CGA graphics, decent for a game made in 1988. The object is to drive forward while shooting or avoiding the obstacles. You do this by pressing right and then hammering on the shoot button. This game was the precursor to the much more widely known Jumpjet which was made by the same company a few years after Offroad.

title: One Must Fall 2097
description: One Must Fall 2097 is a futuristic one-on-one fighting game in the style of other popular fighting games of the time such as Street Fighter II, Mortal Kombat, and numerous others. Upon release, the game was praised for its graphics, smooth gameplay mechanics, and innovative features. Based on the game developer's initial demo, this game takes place far in the future, with mech-like robots fighting each other. There are several game modes: One player vs computer, two player competitive combat, or tournament mode. The last mode is the most innovative: You start by creating your own character to pilot your robot, then gain experience and new powers as you defeat other robots. Sort of like some minor RPG mechanics. Graphically, the game looks good for its time, and the music is pumping, as long as you like early 90's techno! Not the best fighting game ever, but certainly one of the best made for PCs in the 90's. (The game's developer, Diversions Entertainment, released the game as freeware back in 2003 so the download available on DOSGames.com is the full version of the game. A remake project which is open source, OpenOMF, also exists for Windows / other modern OSes.) Video ReviewVideo review of One Must Fall 2097, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Oo-Topos
description: The oddly named Oo-Topos is a sci-fi themed graphical adventure game where you type in simple commands, collect items, and try to figure out what the game expects you to do. It uses the same engine as other Polarware games like Transylvania and The Crimson Crown and likewise features CGA graphics. In the game your space cargo ship has crash-landed on Oo-Topos and you've been taken prisoner. You must escape! LOOK carefully and GET ready to play this fairly typical but professionally done adventure game. Check the official hint guide (PDF) if you get stuck. (This game was originally a commercial game but was released for free by its original authors.)

title: Out of this World (Another World)
description: Out of this World (aka Another World) is a early polygon based action/adventure game which featured a distinctive artistic style and trial-and-error based gameplay which could be rather frustrating, yet the game was certainly memorable and entertaining. You play a scientist who has accidentally been sent to "another world" and must figure out what to do in order to survive. The side-view gameplay feels quite a bit like Prince of Persia, but the gameplay revolves more around simple puzzles. Unless you're using a walkthough, you will undoubtedly die many times as you attempt to figure out where to go and what to do. Later games like Flashback (also made by Delphine) and Blackthorne by Blizzard expanded on this style of game and added additional features, but this was the first. I suspect its artistic style continues to impact games today, especially in the indie scene.

title: Outburst - The Game of Topics
description: Outburst is a board game, originally developed in 1986, that seems similar to the still-popular Family Feud game show. A topic/category is shown, and the participant(s) must guess the top answers related to that topic. This text-mode DOS version allows two players to go head-to-head, or allows a single player to challenge the computer with varying difficulty settings. A sample topic is "PARTS OF A TACO" of which includes the shell, cheese, meat, etc. The game works pretty well, although it shows you the topic before the timer starts with an opportunity to pass, which allows you unlimited time to think of answers before starting the timer, so the timer is basically useless.

title: Outfox
description: Outfox is a computerized version of the old "Fox and Hounds" board game, which was often played using a normal checkers/chess board. This version automates movement of the fox (the computer moves it, so it's one player only), greatly expands the board, and adds various obstacles to complicate matters. The goal is to use your twenty hounds to surround the fox on all eight sides before the fox reaches the bottom of the screen. This is difficult, especially since the fox can sometimes "kick" rocks (?) changing the layout of the map or even taking out one of the hounds. As with most of the author's games, it uses text mode.

title: Pac PC
description: He's a classic symbol (an icon, if you will) for video gaming ... and now you can play an almost arcade perfect version of the Pac-Man arcade game on your computer! In case you need a quick refresher: Pac-Man was one of the first hit arcade games where you collect dots and avoid ghosts in a maze. Pac PC is one of several terrific clones of the classic arcade game, including nearly identical sounds, graphics, and gameplay! The screen scrolls to follow the action. Very impressive indeed.

title: Packman
description: Packman is, as its name suggests, an overt Pac-Man clone. The playing field is horizontal rather than vertical, and the colors are uglier than its arcade counterpart, but it plays competently enough, at least for a game distributed for free in 1983. As in the original game, you control "Packman" and gobble dots while avoiding ghosts. You can gobble a power pellet to turn the tables and eat the ghosts. You move slower while gobbling pellets. Don't expect any fancy features or arcade-accuracy but it's a game that some people will remember from their childhood.

title: Paranoid
description: Paranoid is another ball & paddle game. It features EGA graphics, PC speaker sound effects, and powerups to collect. The game is not particularly exciting to play, and part of that is due to the keyboard-only controls. Your paddle moves at a set speed, and you need to use the left and right shift keys to move. So you need to constantly be tracking the ball, otherwise you may not have time to get to it. The ball DOES bounce off the paddle differently depending where it hits, so that's a big plus. The designs of the levels don't seem particularly inspired, but at least it has a variety of powerups, although they should probably drop more often.

title: Pea Shootin Pete
description: If you've played Spitwad Willy, you've played Pea Shootin' Pete. While I'm not entirely sure about the history of this game, it seems as though after Raoul Said created Spitwad Willy, he either licensed it to Pack Media Company under a new name, or rebranded it when be became involved somehow with the company. Anyways, other than that, it's pretty much the same game, and as such still borrows heavily from Pang (aka Buster Bros). Still fun to play, though as mentioned if you've already played Spitwad Willy it becomes rather unnecessary.

title: Pentix
description: Pentix is a Tetris-like game in text-mode which features oddly-shaped pieces which make it much harder to play. You choose your starting level and then you're off, likely to frustration because the larger pieces don't fit together well, and there is no key to speed up the dropping pieces without dropping them fully, so sliding pieces under other pieces to make them fit is just painful.

title: Perestroika
description: Also known as Toppler, this Russian made game (with text in Russian, but its not really necessary to play the game) was apparently made, in part, as a social political commentary. Right, whatever, it's a fun game to play. The object is to hop across rapidly sinking and reappearing lily pads, collecting bonus tokens and eventually making it to the last golden coin (?) token, and moving on to the next level. Strangely entertaining!

title: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure
description: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure is a simple game aimed at young children. You control Peter Pan as he goes on an adventure and encounters a variety of different challenges. You interact by choosing an action that one of the four "Paintbox Pals" at the bottom of the screen suggests to help Peter get out of trouble. All of the actions are valid and will work, so there's not really any challenge to the game, it's more like a "Choose Your Own Adventure" where all of the options win. It might be fun for small kids because the production values are high. This demo provides an intro animated sequences with voiceover and a few scenes from the full game.

title: Pharaoh's Tomb
description: It's a classic! Apogee Software (who went on to publish Commander Keen, Duke Nukem, and many other famous games) published Pharaoh's Tomb first. It's a platform/puzzle game that's low on action and high on tricky jumps and movements. Clearly some influence from games like Montezuma's Revenge and Rick Dangerous. It admittedly has poor CGA graphics and annoying PC speaker sound effects and one-hit deaths ... but it's still cool as a classic platform jumping game. The full version of this game game has been released for free. Video ReviewVideo review of Pharaoh's Tomb, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Pinball Fantasies
description: Pinball Fantasies is one of a series of several PC pinball games which feature detailed graphics, good music and realistic physics. (This one is a sequel to Pinball Dreams.) This demo version of the full game allows you to play for 10 minutes before the game shuts down. The single table available (Partyland) has a strange carnival/circus theme with bright colors and sound effects. It's fun to play, although I prefer the Epic/Extreme Pinball series personally.

title: Pipe Dream
description: Also known as Pipe Mania or Pipemania, this game about connecting pipes to allow liquids to flow freely spawned a huge number of imitators. Actually I don't know if Pipe Dream is the first of this kind of game, but it's probably the most well-known. This demo version allows you to choose one of three levels from the full game, each with its own custom tileset. The game looks great, and plays well, allowing use of the keyboard or mouse to place your pieces. Note that the bottom piece in the queue is the piece you're placing!

title: Pizza Worm
description: A "worm" style game similar to the QBasic classic "Nibbles". You play a worm who is in search of pizza. It plays much the same as other worm games, except for the fact that you aren't restricted to movement at 90 degree angles. It looks pretty good, and has some SB sounds and music. (Although the music that stops and goes during gameplay may get annoying ...)

title: Plundermine
description: Action-puzzle games are faily rare, but this one probably could qualify as both. The goal is to collect as much gold and silver as possible before the other players (other humans or computer controlled) and avoiding blowing yourself up or getting blown up by the other players. It's a slickly produced game with crisp VGA graphics and a nice tutorial at the beginning to explain how to play. It also supports up to three players, but players 2-3 must use a joystick or gamepad of some type.

title: POD
description: POD is a simple puzzle game where the object is to traverse over all of the tiles on the board without falling off. (No relation to the UBI Soft game released in 1997!) Tiles disappear after you step off them, so you'll need to plan your route carefully. However you can't wait too long, because there's a timer counting down as well! Some tiles also need to be stepped on multiple times before they disappear: Green require two steps, cyan require three. And purple tiles will warp you to another place in the level. There are 20 levels included in the shareware version. The graphics are basic but clean and effective. Probably fun if you enjoy puzzle games.

title: Popcorn
description: Popcorn is a famous Arkanoid clone created in 1988 by a pair of French developers, Christophe Lacaze (code) and Frédérick (graphics/.sounds). This CGA Arkanoid clone was quite popular back in the early DOS days and was widely distributed online, for good reason! It plays quite well, and simulates most of the features of Arkanoid, albeit in CGA mode. The goal is the same: Break all the bricks on the level to progress. There are 50 levels in all, plus a level editor to create your own. The text of the game is in French but it's not too difficult to figure out what's what. (See Instructions for a list of all the function keys.) Note that pressing F9 toggles sound on/off! Full instructions in English can be found in the POP_ENG.DOC file translated by Phillip Bogle. (DOSBox is set to run in CGA mode, which displays the game with its intended RED color rather than the more typical CGA pink. If you're used to playing it in pink, run DOSBox in a VGA mode instead via the "machine" setting in dosbox.conf.) Video ReviewVideo review of Popcorn, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Powball
description: Powball is a nice looking Arkanoid clone. There are various types of blocks to break, various powerups, and a generally appealing interface. The action can get somewhat hectic, what with the explosions and such, especially in two-player mode. You can also use the mouse to move around, which is always a bonus in Arkanoid games. (So much easier than the keyboard!) Overall a well put together game. This game was released as freeware as of July 2000. A new improved version for Windows called Powball Deluxe was released in 2016, also for free.

title: Powerslave
description: Powerslave (also known as "Exhumed") is a FPS built using the Build engine (an the engine used to create Duke Nukem 3D). This demo version displays its distinct Egyptian theme and because it uses the Build engine it plays reasonably well. The graphics and sounds are decent, but it seems to be lacking a bit of the ineffable quality that made Duke so great. (Well, besides the immorality). It plays decently well so if you enjoy 3D shooting games this might be one to try.

title: Pray for Death
description: Pray for Death is a one-on-one fighting game which tries to transfer some of the excitement from arcade beat-em-ups like the popular Street Fighter II, Mortal Kombat, and in this case perhaps most directly Killer Instinct games to the PC platform. The game looks good but as with a lot of this sort of fighting games on PC, the gameplay suffers a bit. There is a wide variety of fighters (although only two are available to select in this demo version) and plenty of special moves and fatalities for each character. Getting them to work if you're just using a keyboard might be a challenge! See the Move list on GameFAQs to learn the special moves for the characters.

title: Prehistorik 2
description: Prehistorik 2 is a platforming game with simple controls and gameplay, but a lot of polish. You are a caveman and need to bonk enemies with your club and collect everything you see for POINTS. The graphics are well-done and the game controls quite smoothly, with the exception being that instead of scrolling smoothly, the levels scroll in screen-sized increments. It's a bit disorienting but not game-breaking. This demo version was updated, perhaps by one of its original programmers, ripsaw8080, to work in DOSBox. It's definitely worth trying out.

title: Prince of Persia
description: Prince of Persia is a classic platforming game developed by Jordan Mechner. It premiered Jordan's use of the "rotoscoping" technique to digitize lifelike movements of the in-game characters. The game itself is a race against time since the clock is always ticking down, but moreso against all of the various traps and high falls in the dungeon which kill you just as much as the enemy characters that you will encounter. As an in-game text file included with the demo states: "It's like an Arabian Nights movie come to life... with you as the star!" The controls do take some getting used to, but they became standard for this sort of game, as also seen in the sequel Prince of Persia: The Shadow and the Flame, as well as other later games like Blackthorne or Out of this World. The graphics are indeed very appealing, as the movements of the characters and other in-game elements feel like they have real weight to them. Try this demo version out to see how you like the original game that inspired the modern 3D series!

title: Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame
description: This is the demo (ie. limited trial) version of the sequel to the classic "Prince of Persia" game. It involves more of the same running, jumping, swordfighting action that you enjoyed in the original game. Despite the nice smooth graphics (using the same "rotoscoping" technique pioneered in the original game), music, sound fx, varied locations, and cult-like status, this game an be very annoying at times with one-hit deaths and controls that take some practice to get used to.

title: Purple Martians
description: Purple Martians is a platforming game, described by its author as being "like Bubble Bobble or Mario". I disagree with that assessment, but it's still a decently fun game. The goal is to get to the exit, blasting baddies on the way. You'll need to destroy all enemies on the level before making it to the exit. They will drop powerups to help you. Although the game's graphics are not the highest quality, they do have a sort of charm about them. And the game itself plays well and offers 35 levels, and even includes a level editor (separate from the main game program) so you can make your own levels.

title: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon
description: Putt-Putt Goes to the Moon is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. Your goal is to find the pieces to put together a space ship to send Putt-Putt back to Earth. Children can click around on many objects to see short animated clips play. Putt-Putt and the rest of the characters are fully voiced, so even kids who aren't strong readers yet will be able to play the game. This game seems like it would still be a lot of fun for kids with its colorful graphics and interaction.

title: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade
description: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade is the first in a long series of Putt-Putt games which are still being released over 20 years later. The game is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. You play the titular car, Putt-Putt, who wants to join the parade. But first he must earn cash to pay for a car wash, among other assorted tasks. There are plenty of things for kids to click on which result in little animation / sound flourishes. The game is designed to use speech instead of text (good for younger players) so be sure to turn on your speakers.

title: Quake
description: One of the best DOS games ever? Probably! Released as the long-awaited follow up to iD Software's classic DOOM, Quake had high expectations. In most ways, I think it met them. Or at least it met mine. It added fully 3D levels, cool new weapons and enemies, and ultra-fast frantic gameplay. And a lot of the color brown. I have spent many hours playing this classic, and still go back to play it sometimes. If you have never played it ... get it now! With the release of Quake, iD Software once again revolutionized the 3D shooting genre. It's great, even today! Video ReviewVideo review of Quake, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Quarantine
description: Quarantine is a futuristic taxi simulation game that predates the Crazy Taxi and Grand Theft Auto series by several years. The game takes place in the gritty futuristic prison city Kemo. The goal is simply to pick up passengers and deliver them to their destinations to earn cash to buy better upgrades for your car. There are missions in the full game, but in this demo you get one of five city districts to explore and pick up passengers, but you can't progress in the game beyond buying new weapons and such. Decent graphics and innovative gameplay for the time.

title: Quato
description: If you're hunting for an enjoyable word game, this could be it. While I have never played "Boggle", this game looks lot like it. The premise is simple: you have three minutes to shift the letters around in a 5x5 grid and create as many words as possible. Points are awarded and the high scores are recorded. The wordlist supposedly contains over 80,000 words. It would be a good idea to force players to look up words in the dictionary that they don't know, because I sometimes spelled words by accident while moving around the tiles! :)

title: Ragnarok
description: Another "roguelike" role-playing game (called "Valhalla" in some regions), Ragnarok gets extra points for using actual graphics instead of the usual ASCII characters used in most other similar games. The gameplay of Ragnarok involves exploring the gameworld, building experience, collecting items, etc ... all of which (like Rogue, Nethack, etc.) are randomly generated each time you begin a new game. The story is also a bit deeper than most games of this type, and you can use your mouse to control some aspects of the game. The motif is also unique, with a Viking/Norse (Scandinavian) mythology rather than the typical fantasy tropes.

title: Rags to Riches: The Financial Market Simulation
description: Rags to Riches is a simulation of being a stock broker, circa the early 90's. You start off with some cash, and you need to use your limited funds to buy investments and hire people to help you. By shrewdly investing, you can make lots of money and go on shopping trips to spend your $$$. This demo version gives you limited options (you can only hire a secretary and a pit runner) but you can get a taste of how the full game will play. (Tip: To hire your first employees, make sure J.E.A is selected on the Rolodex, then click the phone. Then click on the left sidebar to choose who you want to hire.)

title: Raptor: Call of the Shadows
description: I remember playing this for far too long. It's a fairly basic shooting game (gameplay-wise), however, it has nice looking graphics and SB sound effects. As you earn money for each enemy that you blast, you can use the cash to buy upgrades for your ship. This helps to give you an incentive to keep playing and collecting more money and more upgrades to power up your ship. It's enjoyable if you just feel like blasting stuff. It has a very good "feel" to it which has made it a favorite in the shoot-em-up genre. Video ReviewVideo review of Raptor, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Rayman
description: This four-level demo version of the original Rayman game shows off the whimsical graphical style and engaging gameplay of the first game in the series. A villain known as Mr. Dark has captured Rayman's friends, and it's up to you to save them as you travel through platforming levels filled with gorgeous graphics and fluid animations. Rayman has no arms or legs, but he does have hands and feet, which he can use to defeat enemies and grab onto things. You will of course also find powerups along the way. The controls are tight and responsive, and this game is a great introduction to the series which is tons of fun. If you are only familiar with the Rabbids, give the original game a try! For a PC game in 1995 it holds its own compared to the console games of the time.

title: Rebel Decade Chess
description: Unlike some incarnations of chess on the PC, the oddly named "Rebel Decade Chess" program is a hardcore chess simulation. It has a usable interface, but some people who are not hardcore chess players will be a bit overwhelmed by all of the options. I'm only a casual player (that is to say, I suck) so I can't really judge how good the computer is ... it whupped me pretty soundly though. :) The developer released several other versions of this game on their website if you're interested in more modern versions.

title: RetroFuel
description: Thiago Marques, author of the fantastic modern DOS game Death Taxi 3000, created RetroFuel for the DOS Games Spring Jam 2020. It is a 3D racing game which plays similarly to Lotus, Outrun, and other classic arcade racers. This is an unfinished version of the game, hence the "demo" tag. So far it has three tracks and plays quite well! The best way to support development of this game is to purchase the full version of Death Taxi 3000 if you enjoy either game!

title: Revenge of the Mutant Camels
description: A side-scrolling platforming shooting game from Jeff Minter's Llamasoft? It must be incredibly zany! With a name like Revenge of the Mutant Camels, that's pretty much a given. Here you pilot your goat riding a mutant camel as it runs from left to right, shooting in whichever direction you last moved, sorta like a Robotron / Llamatron platforming game. Things attack you from all angles and you try to retain your sanity as you try to shoot them. Graphics and sounds are also suitably zany. It's definitely an interesting experience but I personally didn't find it particularly fun to play!

title: Rise Of The Triad
description: A decent and relatively unknown FPS from Apogee. (Unknown compared to Wolf3D, DOOM, Duke, etc.) It's sort of in-between Wolf3D and Duke3D. It has some cool new features, such as choosing different characters at the beginning of the game, each of whom has unique abilities. But at times they don't seem to work together all that well. For example, there's too much platform jumping. Some people love this game, presumably due to its aesthetic, but I personally wasn't that excited about it. It doesn't feel as smooth as Doom. Some great ideas here though, and definitely unique. Video ReviewVideo review of Rise Of The Triad, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Robod
description: Robod is a 3D-perspective action game similar to Wolfenstein-3D or Blake Stone except that it was made over 22 years after those games. Created by mar and draxx for the hvdosdev 22 Czech DOS game dev jam on high-voltage.cz. The game itself is pretty simple, run around the maze and destroy the evil robots. You can use modern WASD + mouse controls or more old-school arrow keys if you prefer. The graphics are decent, chiptune-ish music is good, and the game overall is fun to play, so give it a try. There's also a Windows executable included.

title: Robots the Game
description: Robots the Game (or simply "BOT" on the title screen) is a simple chase game done in text mode (except the title screen) which plays similarly to Autobots and others games like it. The object is to make the robots crash into each other; they will relentlessly chase you, and you'll need to move carefully (and use your limited "jumps" which move you to a random location) to destroy them all and move on to the next level.

title: Rock Rush Xmas Edition
description: This Xmas themed version of RockRush doesn't really add too much to the game. Your character from the original game has been transformed into Santa! And the title screen is Christmas themed, and the graphics have a little seasonal holiday quality to them. But I can't imagine that this special edition of the game took too much effort to put together except for one detail that I'll mention shortly. Regardless, if you enjoy Boulderdash games, you'll likely still enjoy this version of the Boulderdash clone. it also includes a level editor to create your own levels, which I guess would be the main draw here.

title: RockRush
description: Boulderdash is a game that, for whatever reason, has inspired legions of clones over the years. I am not personally a huge fan, but people must enjoy the game since there are so many versions of it available! RockRush is another such game, with some decent graphics which change depending on which "cave" of levels you select. Functionally it works the same as Boulderdash, such that you simply use the arrow keys to move around the mazes, collecting rainbow-colored gems and avoiding getting crushed by the boulders or other traps.

title: Rocks'n'Diamonds
description: Rocks'n'Diamonds is at its core a Boulderdash clone, but it's so much more than that! It comes with a huge collection of levels culled from other games; you get all of the levels from Boulderdash, Emerald Mine, Sokoban, and Supaplex. Plus it includes a level editor so you can create your own unique levels using any of the assets from those games. There also many additional levels available in case the hundreds that it comes with aren't enough! The graphics are well-drawn tiles at 800x600 resolution and the game includes MOD-style music as well. A great achievement and amazing amount of content available for free! (The game is continuing to receive updates, but only to the Windows and other more modern platforms: Recent versions of Rocks'n'Diamonds.)

title: Rogue
description: The original "Roguelike"! It may have primitive graphics (ASCII), and no sound, but it's still quite enjoyable. People love these sorts of games because they're so indepth, and different every time you play. Check out this one to see a piece of gaming history, or are looking for a simpler alternative to super-indepth games like Nethack or ADOM ... but generally I still prefer Nethack. (This version was adapted for PC by Jon Lane.) Video ReviewVideo review of Rogue, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games
publisher: Micheal Toy, Glenn Wichman, & Kenneth Arnold

title: Rooms of the Abyss
description: Rooms of the Abyss is a basic first-person perspective dungeon crawling game. Your quest is to ... well there's a long story in the MANUAL.TXT file (which you may want to look at anyways for gameplay controls / tips) but it doesn't really matter. You need to wander through the dungeons, slaying monsters, finding keys, and unlocking doors until you find your way to the next level. There is an automap feature which is nice. However the combat seems pretty basic and uninteresting. The graphics draw slowly using basic shapes, so the gameplay proceeds slowly as well. Also, it took me a few moments to realize that the left and right arrows actually make your character STRAFE and not TURN, so you can't actually TURN AROUND in this game. You just go forward, back, and side to side! Weird. One of the authors has released the full version for free and so you can download / play the registered version here.

title: Sam & Max: Hit the Road
description: Sam & Max features a detective dog and "hyperkinetic" rabbit in a graphical adventure game. This is one of the classic Lucasarts games, coming around the same time as other classics like Day of the Tentacle. The story involves the two protagonists traveling across America to solve their case. Along the way you will encounter numerous puzzles that you solve via the Lucasarts point-and-click adventure interface, as well as a few mini games. The game excels in its irreverent humor and the dialogue between Sam and Max and other characters. The graphics, music, and sound effects are all top-notch, so be sure to check out this game if you're a fan of graphical adventure games. Note that the demo only allows you to play through a few screens before ending. Video ReviewVideo review of Sam & Max, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Sango Fighter
description: Sango Fighter is a game that looks better than it actually plays. Inspired by the extremely popular Street Fighter series of games (and the dozens of clones that SF2 inspired) Sango Fighter likewise features detailed and interesting looking characters fighting in one-on-one combat. Each character has unique special moves; however they are not easy to pull off. The shareware version allows you to select one of five fighters, and play in tournament, battle, and two player vs modes. As stated above, although this game looks great. The sounds and music are decent as well. However the gameplay is a little choppy, and it's not too easy to pull off the characters' special moves. That, combined with only having 5 playable characters, make it much less fun than SF2 which it's emulating. Definitely worth trying out though as an example of what was possible in the early 90's DOS environment compared to the arcades of the era. (Sango Fighter features English, Chinese, and Japanese language options.) Video ReviewVideo review of Sango Fighter, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Scorched Earth
description: The best tank war game I've ever seen. It's called 'The Mother of all games' by the author and was chosen as PC World magazine as the third best DOS game of all time. In it, you are competing against up to 10 other tanks (controlled by other players or by the computer) and you battle by entering a velocity and turret angle before firing off various weapons, which you can purchase between rounds. Your weapons available to buy include Nukes, Napalm, Smoke Tracers, and Liquid Dirt, among many others. It looks and plays great, and it's great fun blowing up a tiny little tank with a huge nuke. (There are several levels of computer AI available, however you generally choose from "dumb as a doornail" to "nearly perfect" ...) Video ReviewVideo review of Scorched Earth, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Screamer
description: Screamer is a 3D perspective arcade-style racing game. By arcade-style I mean that it is not particularly realistic but it does move fast and feature big crashes. You're racing against nine opponents on the included track in this demo version of the game; no options to set, just race and repeat if you'd like. The full game has a bunch of car options and tracks to select, but here you can just admire the graphics (non-3D accelerator) and sounds. It runs fairly smoothly so should be good for racing game fans.

title: SDI2040
description: SDI2040 is a Space Invaders clone. It doesn't add many new features. There are some subtle differences, like the fact that the enemy ships are smaller than usual so they are a bit trickier to hit. The game plays decently, and includes functional graphics and sound effects, but nothing particularly exciting. The controls may take some getting used to, since your ship will continue to move in one direction unless you hit the down key or move the opposite way.

title: SEAL Team
description: SEAL Team is a Vietnam War strategy / action game. You control a single soldier, who gives orders to your teammates. As part of the team, you also move your own character, and attempt to complete the level's objective(s), such as killing all of the enemies, rescuing a hostage, or recovering an object. The game is presented from a third person perspective in full 3D using polygons to model the environments. (Supposedly using the same engine as 688 Attack Sub.) It looks impressive, but the action is a bit slower paced since this is supposed to be a sim / action hybrid type game. Definitely worth a look if you enjoy games of this sort.

title: Secret Agent
description: A fun platform game from Apogee which includes a lot of gameplay value. This game uses the same engine (and some of the same gameplay devices) as Crystal Caves, also from Apogee, however this game was a bit dated (technology-wise) upon its release and was largely overlooked. Still, it's EGA graphics are decent to look at and don't distract from the game. This game has you playing as "Agent 006½" (haha) and exploring technology-themed espionage levels. Definitely recommended if you enjoy Apogee's other famous games. A remake of this game was recently released by Apogee themselves! Check it out on GOG.com! Video ReviewVideo review of Secret Agent, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Seek and Destroy
description: Seek and Destroy is an entertaining and well polished shooting game. Using superb VGA graphics and SB sound effects, the object of the game is to complete missions using either a chopper or a tank (your choice before each mission begins). The game controls fairly well and the battlefields smoothly rotate 360 degrees around your chosen battle machine. Quite a well done game overall, although it seems like for some reason it was not generally well known upon its release. Video ReviewVideo review of Seek & Destroy, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Shadow Warrior
description: Created using the "Build" engine (the same software the Duke Nukem 3D was created with), Shadow Warrior was largely ignored upon its release due to the fact that Quake has been released the year before, with superior graphics and gameplay enhancements (true 3D environments). Shadow Warrior is still a great game, with many of the same gameplay elements that make Duke Nukem 3D such a classic game, although some of the "off-color humor" might be offensive to some gamers.

title: Shards
description: Shards is a puzzle game that involves matching sets of tiles with symbols on them. You'll need to move your ball around the levels, trying to get tiles to match, while probably struggling with the controls a bit in the beginning. "All the keys you'll need" are cursors to move, Spacebar to toggle the "cross wires" and M to toggle "stone-move-mode", but the way the game works is not intuitive, at least not for me. The graphics are alright, but I'm not really a fan of the two songs which only play during the levels, of which there are only 10 in the shareware version. (There are 60 levels in the full registered version.)

title: Sherlock
description: In this game you must use your powers of deduction to determine the positions of images in an array. The various kinds of clues may take some effort to learn, but the game includes built-in instructions. Much like many puzzle games, only average graphics, but since this game is quite unique and plays well you may enjoy it. A must for logic puzzle fans. There is also a modern Windows version of the game available.

title: Silencer
description: Silencer is a simple action / strategy game where the goal is to crush ("silence") your enemies by pushing around blocks. It's similar to William Soleau's The Crusher and Crusher Castle 2 although there's probably no direct influence. There are seven different enemies to "silence" as you traverse the fifteen levels of the game, each with their own patterns to deal with. It's a decent game with responsive controls; make sure NUM LOCK is on so you can move diagonally with your numeric keypad. (You DO have a numeric keypad, right? Sorry laptop users, this game will be tough without one ...)

title: Simcity
description: This time-limited demo version of the original Simcity shows off a little of what made the game so revolutionary at the time. The game does not play like a traditional video game in the sense that there is no definite "win" condition; your goal is to simply build the best city that you can. The series began a whole line of "Sim" games which were essentially sandbox titles. The original is simple compared to other games in the series but part of its charm is the simplicity which makes it easy to learn. The graphics are serviceable, and while there is no background music, the simple PC speaker sound effects are quite memorable. Video ReviewVideo review of Simcity, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Simcity 2000
description: Simcity 2000 is of course the sequel to the immensely popular Simcity which Maxis released a few years earlier in 1989. This demo version of the sequel (limited to 20 minutes of playing time) keeps many of the same gameplay mechanics as the original, but also improves the graphics and sounds while implementing new mechanics to build your own cities. You are again the mayor of a new city, and your task is to grow it into a healthy metropolis. There are of course many new buildings that you can create such as zoos and hospitals. The land is now no longer completely flat, so you may need to do some terraforming to be able to place things where you want them. Some of the new mechanics seem a bit unnecessary and tedious (such as the water system) while other such as the newspapers provided to gauge how your city is doing are nice additions. Generally speaking a great sequel to the original, although the original game is still a better choice for a more casual experience.

title: Simon the Sorcerer
description: Simon the Sorcerer is a classic graphical adventure game, and one of the few well-known games of its type from its time that was not released by Sierra or Lucasarts. The plot follows the titular Simon, an average English boy who ends up being teleported into a magical land and must become a sorcerer's apprentice. The style of the game is quite similar to Lucasarts titles such as Secret of Monkey Island, in both gameplay and its comedic tone. There are numerous parodies of fairytales in the game. Generally speaking the game features great graphics and music, as well as an enjoyable puzzle-solving experience. Try this demo version to see if you like it before buying the full version! (Apparently the version on GOG.com is not good; try buying it from the original publisher instead.)

title: Sir Addalot's "Mini" Math Adventure
description: Sir Addalot is a children's math game. The goal is to stop the evil dragon Scorch from terrorizing the kingdom. To do so, you, brave Sir Addalot, must match equal mathematical expressions, as knights of old often did. The game has decent graphics, as well as PC speaker "music" (you may want to turn it off in the options menu). Keyboard and mouse controls are provided. The game generally plays well, although the action the player takes is identical throughout the entire game, even though you move to different "castles" you still do the exact same thing. There are difficulty levels however so once a child starts getting bored you could turn up the challenge. (Bonus: See a scan of the magazine ad for this game courtesy of Mobygames!)

title: Ski Jump International
description: This game simulates the ski jump event, an olympic event which I was personally never much interested in, but this athletic competition has been transformed into a realistic game of reflexes and timing. The object is simply to jump as far as possible, over some nicely drawn winter landscapes. The keyboard keys used for the jumping process are rather complicated, so make sure to read the instructions before playing. (The game was originally shareware but has been released by its author as freeware.)

title: SkyRoads: Xmas Special
description: SkyRoads: Xmas Special is a holiday themed release of the original Skyroads game which is an action/arcade 3D "racing" game where the only goal is to safely finish the course. You get unlimited retries to finish each course, which is a good thing because they can be very difficult! In this release, four holiday-themed sets of courses replace four in the original game. From what I've seen (and from the comments of others) these new courses are not as enjoyable as the courses in the original game, despite their cheery festive designs!

title: SLASH
description: SLASH is a variant of Nethack, one of the most popular old roguelike games. SLASH stands for "SuperLotsaAddedStuffHack" and true to its name (which may be a backronym) it adds a bunch of stuff and makes a bunch of changes. Based on v3.1.3 of Nethack, and including features from other hacks NetHack Plus and NetHack--, it adds roles, monsters, items, custom dungeon levels, and more. Worth a look if you like Nethack. If you don't like Nethack, don't bother with this!

title: Sleuth
description: If you're looking for a very original puzzle game, this one could be it. Sleuth involves attempting to solve a murder mystery, by exploring a house and questioning suspects. The graphics may be crude by today's standards (good 'ol DOS ASCII) the game itself is very cool. It's different every time you play, plus you can add your own name in (or the names of your friends) as the suspects. Neat!

title: SlipSpeed
description: It's 2020 and new amazing MS-DOS games continue to be released! SlipSpeed is a game that includes elements from many games, but may remind players of the popular Super Sprint game. (Or its MS-DOS shareware clone, Super Speed. It's a racing game where you race your Slip-craft through 16 levels of drifting action. Since you're flying (hovering?) the steering is a lot floatier than most driving games but it works well here. The graphics and sounds are great and add a lot to the experience. The full version is available on itch.io.

title: Snack Attack!
description: Snack Attack! is a Pac-Man clone. While not 100% finished, and intended as a demo of the author's Euphoria programming language book / course, it is still quite playable. It includes the typical Pac-Man intro music and sound effects, and four quirky ghosts that chase you around the maze. The ghosts do appear to move intelligently, although I'm not an expert so I don't know if they move in the same patterns as the original arcade game. Overall it's not a bad version of Pac-Man, although there are better clones available.

title: Snipes
description: This simple text mode action game with simple but enjoyable Gauntlet-like gameplay. You're in a maze, and you need to find and destroy the enemy generators, which spit out ASCII smiley-faced enemies that attack you. Not too intense of a game, but it has some interesting origins: It was apparently commissioned by Novell to test the networking capabilities of early LANs. So this game from 1982 has networked multiplayer capabilities, but don't ask me how to get it to work!

title: Snood
description: Even though Snood was basically a weird looking takeoff of the popular Puzzle Bobble or Bust-A-Move, it became extremely popular for a time. The object, like Puzzle Bobble, is to rotate your turret at the bottom of the screen and shoot colored "Snoods" to try to connect three or more of the same color. The Snoods themselves are rather ugly face-blocks of different colors. Every time you shoot a Snood and don't make a three-or-more connection the Danger meter increases, and when it's full the screen drops by one. The graphics are detailed (high-res 640x480 mode) and certainly distinct, but strange, and the gameplay is classic but also a bit simple by today's standards.

title: Sokoball of Osaka
description: Sokoball of Osaka is, as you might expect, a version of the classic Sokoban block-pushing puzzle game. This version has the same goal (get all of the blocks to the target(s), here they are "exit shafts") but also includes other kinds of tiles, like one-way tiles and levels that change their layout when a certain tile is stepped on. The gameplay generally works well, although the graphical style make distinguishing the different tiles a bit difficult. A total of 18 puzzles are included in the shareware version along with an editor to create your own puzzles. The included puzzles are all rather difficult so this game will be a good choice if you're looking for a challenge.

title: Sokoban 3D
description: Sokoban 3D is an interesting idea for a game that just doesn't work well in practice. Sokoban of course is the classic block-pushing game of which there are many variations. The goal is to push all of the blocks onto the markers. Blocks can only be pushed, not pulled, and only one block may be pushed at a time. This version is in 3D, which makes it very difficult to visualize the layout of the level, and even to know exactly where you're standing in relation to the blocks. There is a map mode if you hit Tab but you can't move in that mode. It's probably more fun to play another non-3D Sokoban game, the novelty of 3D wears off quite quickly.

title: Sokoland
description: Sokoland is a version of the classic Sokoban game which includes the 50 levels from the original game, as well as a level editor to make your own levels or sets of levels. If you've never played Sokoban, the object is to push the blocks onto the markers. The tricky part is pushing all the blocks without getting any stuck in unmovable positions. There isn't much here to speak about other than the level editor; unfortunately user-created levels seem to be gone (even from Wayback Machine) so you probably won't find any new levels floating around out there on the web.

title: Solar Winds: The Escape
description: I had a bit of a problem putting this game in a category, since it includes quite a bit of adventure elements along with the shooting. You become a space pilot who is sent on various missions, and to complete them you must sometimes destroy another ship (or many ships) or sometimes simply pickup an item, or talk to the captain of another ship. The different genres gel well together, and the game includes smooth-scrolling VGA graphics. A bit like Star Control, I think. I've never really played Star Control, but it seems similar. :)

title: Sopwith
description: A true classic! :) Despite its CGA 4-color graphics, Sopwith is a game that many of you have probably played at one time or another. In this game you fly your plane around a landscape, and use your guns and bombs to blow up targets on the ground and in the air. It's still good fun if you look past the dated graphics/sounds! This is the "Network Edition" but don't ask me how to get it working over a network. (Note: This version is slightly modified from the original by the original author of the game so that it will work with modern computers.) More info and downloads of other versions are available on the sopwith.org website. NOTE! Controls: X starts the engine, then press , to go up, / to go down, Spacebar to fire, and B to drop bombs.

title: Space Invaders
description: Space Invaders is not surprisingly a clone of the classic Space Invaders arcade game. This one is not made by Taito, rather by Paul S Reid, who was at the time working on a comp sci diploma, as per the included docs. It's a decent approximation of the arcade, although there are no sounds and every time your ship gets destroyed, the aliens all respawn, which is not how it worked in the arcade AFAIK. Still a decent attempt which works more or less like you'd expect, and it's impressive that the executable file is so tiny.

title: Space Pilot
description: Space Pilot is a decent space dogfighting game. The concept is simple: shoot the other ships! The controls are a bit awkward at first (use the Alt/Ctrl keys to rotate and Shift to fire) but aren't so bad once you get used to them. Average graphics, but the game itself seems pretty well put together. A no-frills shooting game with not much to make it remarkable.

title: Spacewar
description: Do you like old games? What about the OLDEST game? Spacewar is generally credited with being the first video game, even before Pong. It was originally created in 1962 by Steve Russell at MIT. This DOS version was released much later, and recreates the original with some modifications. The game is essentially a 1-on-1 fight between two spaceships (2-players on one keyboard or you vs the computer). The graphics and so on are of course very primitive, but download this anyways to experience part of video games history.

title: Spear Of Destiny
description: A sequel of sorts to Wolfenstein 3D that was released by Formgen as a retail only game (not shareware like Wolf3D) this demo version unfortunately contains only two playable levels. However the Spear of Destiny game is still great fun, although it uses the exact same engine, graphics, sounds etc as Wolfenstein 3D and features only new levels, some new bosses, and not much else.

title: Speed Haste
description: Speed Haste is an arcade-style 3D perspective racing game. Choose your car (you only get one in the demo version) then your track (only two in the demo) then race! Or do a Grand Prix if you want. The game plays pretty smoothly, although in my brief time playing I didn't really get the hang of gliding around corners without crashing. I'm sure that'll come if you play for a while. Decent sounds accompany the polygon-filled visuals. The Speed Haste source code has been released if you're interested.

title: Spych
description: This simple block-pushing puzzle game shares many similarities with games such as Sokoban or Boxxle. The object is to push boxes around, onto their proper markers, as well as collect keys and avoid obstacles on the way to the level exit. Although the game's graphics are not very good, it does seem challenging and long, so fans of the genre should be able to play this one for awhile.

title: Squarez Deluxe!
description: An interesting and original puzzle game. It reminds me a bit of Tetris, in that you move around Tetris-style pieces. Your task here, though, is to create 3x3 squares. It isn't as easy as it sounds! Great graphics, a great premise and slick design make this one a keeper! There are also multiple playing modes, including Basic, Normal, and EXTREME modes, as well as two-player head-to-head play.

title: Star Control II: The Ur-Quan Masters
description: Star Control II is considered by many to be one of the greatest PC games of all time. (Even in 2018 it was voted as the top PC game ever in a large online poll.) The game is a space exploration / combat simulation with a deep story and a huge world to explore. There is a plethora of worlds to visit and quests to complete, along with an engaging plotline. Your interactions with various species allow you to form alliances which are important for completing the game. While most of the game is leisurely paced, combat turns into an action-packed experience. Definitely worth trying; this demo version gives you a taste of the full version experience. A free open-source Windows port of the full game, based on converted 3DO code released by the developers, is available here: The Ur-Quan Masters. Definitely recommended!NOTE: For the DEMO version of this game you will need to initially run it with DOSBox cycles set 1000! After the main game screen loads, you can increase the cycles to a more reasonable amount like 4000. Otherwise the game will appear too dark! (Press Ctrl-12 to increase the cycles while in-game.) More info Video ReviewVideo review of Star Control 2, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Star Wars: Dark Forces
description: A demo version of one of a simply great 3D shooting game that I missed playing when it was originally released. Also known as "Star Wars: Dark Forces", this 3D shooting game does not use the DOOM engine, it uses LucasArts' own engine which includes a few features not seen in DOOM. (Though it still includes a very DOOM-like map.) Smooth although low-res graphics and responsive gameplay, along with the Star Wars theme, make this one a keeper. Definitely play it if you enjoy 3D shooting games! Video ReviewVideo review of Dark Forces, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Stargunner
description: Stargunner is a little known shooting game (shoot em up) from Apogee, publishers of other great games like Commander Keen, Duke Nukem and (related by genre to Stargunner) Raptor: Call of the Shadows. Stargunner is a bit more simplistic than Raptor, but generally its no less fun to play, and includes decent low-res VGA graphics and booming sound effects. Levels are repetitious but that's somewhat expected from the genre. Overall its a well made shooter for fans of space shooting games along the lines of Gradius or Raiden. (This game has been released as freeware! Enjoy! Note that it's a large file, approx 40MB!) Video ReviewVideo review of Stargunner, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Stone Mist
description: Stone Mist is a classic early Ultima style RPG, complete with turn-based battles and a fairly in-depth character generation system (that must be run separately before running the game). The story is typical fantasy RPG fare, and there are some quirks to the engine, but overall it's a competently presented game with decent VGA graphics. There is an extensive documentation file (SMVOL1.DOC) that you will likely need to reference since the in-game help is minimal. I didn't make it too far into this game but there seems to be a decently large world to explore, and at least you can (usually?) run from battles if you don't want to fight monsters constantly. (Note: The DOSBox version playable online defaults to a sample character I made; download and run the game on your own computer to create your own.)

title: Styx
description: Styx was released by Windmill Software in 1983. It is a decent clone of the arcade game Qix (also sometimes known as "Kix"). This is actually a "remastered" version of the game that has been altered to work a bit better on modern computers. Also the game was originally released bootable floppy only game, but this version works like a normal DOS game. (As usual with really old games, run with DOSBox, otherwise it'll probably run too fast in Windows or not work at all.) NOTE: Move with the arrow keys and hold down the F1 key to move your ball into the center area!

title: Sub Battle Simulator
description: This late 80's demo version of Epyx's Sub Battle Simulator offers CGA submarine simulation action for your enjoyment! It has the same/similar features as the full game but you're limited to a maximum playing time of 5 minutes. The included README.DOC file is REQUIRED reading since it lists the dozens of keyboard keys needed to control your sub. The setting is World War 2, and you'll battle opposing forces including airplanes. This seems like a pretty in-depth simulation, at least based on the number of keys required to play.

title: Subhunt
description: Subhunt is an interesting submarine mission simulation game developed by a group at a university game development lab: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas, which still exists today. Apparently it was coded entirely from scratch using no existing libraries in C++ and Assembly. Anyways, it's a submarine simulator, so there are lots of buttons and things to press, and you'll need to spend some time learning how everything works because this is not an arcade-type sim. It does provide you with a 3D-rendered view outside your sub. The full game contains 12 missions but only one is included in the shareware game.
publisher: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas

title: Supaplex
description: If you're looking for an involving puzzle game (which bears a strong reseblance to the classic game "Boulderdash"), Superplex might be what you're looking for. It recently has been updated to work on modern machines. It features distinctive graphics with a computer-ish theme, and a plehora of precarious puzzles (yay alliteration). The menus are a bit confusing at first but once you get into the game it's great. The version available for download here is a "speed fix" version which was released by Elmer Productions. You can also play a modernized version online at supaplex.online. Video ReviewVideo review of Supaplex, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Super Street Fighter II Turbo
description: Street Fighter II first came to DOS PCs in 1992, with an absolutely terrible port of the original game Street Fighter II: The World Warrior. Thankfully, this version is way better than the original port, making this game quite close to the arcade and console versions of the game. If you've played SF2 before, you know what to expect: One-on-one fighting of the highest quality. Great graphics, sound effects, and music round out the package. Of course using the keyboard to perform special moves is mediocre at best so you'd probably want a joystick or arcade setup if you're interested in playing this for real. The demo version allows play as Ryu and Chun Li only, and while two-player shared keyboard play is available in the full version, the demo is one player only.

title: Syndicate
description: Syndicate is a beloved classic DOS action / strategy game where you play a hit man for one of a handful of global corporations (syndicates) that have taken over the world. Reminiscent of the look of the X-Com games but in real-time, you move your squad of characters through the missions, earning money by successfully completing them to upgrade your team for the next mission. The graphics are great; 640x480 x 16 colors has rarely looked so good. The action can get frantic fast and it'll take some time to learn the controls and how to help your team survive! (This demo contains a single level; the full game has over 50.) Video ReviewVideo review of Syndicate, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: System Shock
description: System Shock was a revolutionary and memorable game that is hard to place in a single genre. It does use a 3D FPS engine similar to other games like DOOM, but it also includes puzzle and RPG elements. The documentation included with the game states: "System Shock is not meant to be DOOM. System Shock is a RPG game for one player only, just like Ultima Underworld, not a multiplayer action game like DOOM." So there you have it, straight from the developers, or perhaps some marketing person, we don't really know. In any case, in System Shock you play a hacker who is trying to stop SHODAN, a futuristic AI gone berserk, from destroying the Earth. The game is immersive as it draws players into its creepy atmosphere. Definitely an influential game that inspired later story-intensive first-person games such as Deux Ex. (This demo version contains the first level of the game.)

title: Tank Wars
description: Tank Wars (also known as BOMB due to the name of the zip file and it's executable file) is, as you might expect, a tank battle game. It is quite similar to the better-known game Scorched Earth which was released around the same time in the early 90's. The goal of the game is to destroy the other tank(s) controlled by human players or computer opponents (of varying intelligence levels) by selecting the angle and velocity of your shots. The game generates terrain of different formations for each level and includes wind as well (both typical of games in this genre, even the famous QBasic Gorillas game) as well as a ton of different configurable options. There are also different weapons that you can purchase between rounds. Generally a fun game of this genre. I have heard that the computer opponents' AI is tuned a bit better than Scorched Earth, so if you're looking to play against your PC (up to 10 simultaneously) this may be your best choice. Video ReviewVideo review of Tank Wars, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Tempest 2000
description: Tempest is a vector-based action / shooting arcade game that was released in 1981. Your ship rotates around the tubular playing field and shoots the enemies as they approach towards the screen. This updated version was released in 1994, with similar gameplay and a freshly updated design by Jeff Minter of Llamasoft fame. (It is known as one of the few good games released primarily for the Atari Jaguar system!) The graphics and sounds ratchet up the intensity level, with pixelated explosions and cycling colors complimenting the smooth vector-like animations. Safe to say that if you enjoyed the original you will like this updated version, presented here in demo form.

title: Terminal Velocity
description: It takes a little while to get used to, but this flying/shooting game (sort of like Decent, but more out in the open) can be really fun to play. (It gets much tougher during the later levels, however.) I found it to be a lot of fun, even though it gets very challenging. The open-ended feeling of flying around is not often found in games of this era. Impressive what could be done back then without the aid of any kind of 3D graphics card! (Note: Microsoft later released this game as a Windows game called 'Fury3'. As far as I know, the games are identical.) Video ReviewVideo review of Terminal Velocity, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Terminator: Rampage
description: Terminator: Rampage is a 3D shooting game from Bethesda, one of several in their early/mid 90's line of Terminator FPS games. Compared to some of the other games in the series, it's not quite up to the same level. The engine is a bit clunky (the game was released just before DOOM but is technically way behind) and the turning speed feels exceedingly slow compared to how fast you move forwards. The level design feels like a confusing maze with walls that are all the same color. There are enemies to fight, and each pops up an information box when you target them which is nice, but really you treat each the same way and shoot them until they blow up.

title: Terminator: SkyNET
description: SkyNET (aka Terminator: SkyNET) is the final of three Terminator based FPS games that Bethesda released in the 90's. It was originally planned as an expansion pack for Terminator: Future Shock, SkyNET was released as a separate game, with an updated version of the 3D engine used. The game is pretty advanced for its time, with many different weapons, enemies, and even vehicles that you can drive. There are a lot of evil robots to destroy and plenty of things to shoot. The demo includes a single level of the 8 missions included in the full game, along with a single multiplayer map.

title: Terroid
description: Ready to shoot stuff? In space? Yep. That's what happens in Terroid. It's a classic R-Type style shooting game where you shoot other ships and pick up powerups. Some parts of this game are a bit strange though. Like why is your ship so big? What do the powerups actually do (most don't seem to do anything)? Why is the music so terrible? Fans of the genre, or classic game competionists, may want to check it out. But it's not a high point in the genre's history. One interesting note is that if you choose "Informations" in the menu you're given a multi-screen backstory for the game, which is often missing from shmups.

title: Tetris
description: The original version of Tetris, as conceived by Alexey Pajitnov and coded in part by Vadim Gerasimov, this is how it all began! (Gerasimov has released the game for free on the web.) The story of Tetris is long and complicated (see the superb hour long video by the Video Game Historian, The Story of Tetris, to learn all about it!) but the game itself is deceptively simple. If you owned an original Gameboy, chances are you played this! This version of the original includes many of the options familiar to us from later versions including Nintendo's. Gerasimov notes that this version was done in text mode in order to be compatible with the widest variety of machines available at the time. (If you're looking for more elaborate Tetris games with better graphics, more features, etc, check out our Tetris-style games category for plenty of options!)

title: Tetris Queen
description: Tetris Queen is a good game for people who enjoy Tetris, a great game for those who like the music of the band Queen (who doesn't?) and an absolutely fantastic game for those who like both. This game offers both classic mode (same as regular Tetris) and destroyer mode (Tetris "WITH BOMBS IN IT"). It also offers a two-player simultaneous mode, along with great graphics and music of some of Queen's greatest hits. (Music obtained from the no longer existing but Archive.org preserved Queen Trivia Quiz website.) The controls are configurable in-game which is always a welcome feature, especially since the defaults didn't work well for me. Overall it's a great version of Tetris!

title: Text-World
description: Text-World is a text adventure game creation system which attempts to simplify the process of creating games compared to other systems like AGT. It provides a menu with various options which allow you to compose your games. It seems as though a variety of options are provided, so this would be good for people wanting to create a simple text game, however more complicated games may not be possible due to the restrictions imposed by this system.

title: The Adventures of Maddog Williams in the Dungeons of Duridian
description: Reminiscent of earlier Sierra (On-Line) games, Maddog Williams employs the same style interface as the original Kings Quest and Space Quest games. (And, uh, Leisure Suit Larry ...) The story, which is explained in a lengthy cinema before the game starts, is pretty standard adventure game fare, but the game is quite well put together. It has some nicely drawn graphics (although they are a bit too dark) and good 'ol fashioned gameplay.

title: The Black Cauldron
description: Adventure game fans may remember this classic graphic adventure game, created by Al Lowe (of "Leisure Suit Larry" fame) and loosely based on the Disney movie of the same name. The gameplay is simplified a bit from most other famous Sierra releases. The game is controlled not controlled by typing commands, everything is done through the function keys (F1,F2,etc). Press F1 during the game for a list of these keys (or check the walkthrough guide below). Overall a simplistic but fun early graphical adventure game. Video ReviewVideo review of The Black Cauldron, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: The Blues Brothers
description: The Blues Brothers, a game based on the Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi Saturday Night Live comedic duo, is a platforming game produced by European developer Titus. The game has nice graphics and sounds, with the graphics having that certain European flavor. You can choose to play as either Jake or Elwood in this demo version of the full five-level game. You have no weapons, but you can pick up and throw crates (ala Super Mario Bros 2, which was released a few years earlier on the NES) to defeat foes that come after you. A decent licensed game.

title: The Incredible Machine
description: This is a demo version of the classic game The Incredible Machine, but it gives new players a taste of what this game has to offer. The game consists of using certain provided objects (gears, wheels, candles, a monkey riding a bicycle ...) to accomplish a certain task (get all the balls into the hoops, scare a cat, pop all the balloons ...) in each level. It's great fun, and so is building your own weird machines in freeform mode (unfortunately disabled in the demo). Thankfully the full version of the game is available online now for purchase in various legal forms so new generations can experience the fun. Video ReviewVideo review of The Incredible Machine, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: The Incredible Machine 2
description: The Incredible Machine was an incredibly (!) fun game which encouraged players to creatively achieve different objectives on each level by building makeshift machines out of peculiar parts. The sequel presents more great puzzles for players to solve, with the same quirky graphical style and music that helped make the first game so memorable. There are plenty of odd parts to play with, such as kettles, computers, cats, blimps, and many more. This demo version gives you a small taste of what the full version has to offer, since there are only 5 playable levels available here.

title: The Last Eichhof
description: The Last Eichhof is a decent game with an ... uh, "original" premise? In this space shooting game, you play a beer floating in space. Yeah, like a bottle of beer. You must shoot down all of the enemies (like kegs and stuff) using an unlimited supply of bottle caps and save the universe (I guess ... why not ...) from big corporations. Aside from the premise, the game does have decent production values, with lots of music and sound effects, and decent graphics with plenty of animation and smooth effects. You can also buy upgrades between levels. (Note that to exit the store you must move ALL THE WAY LEFT to the green EXIT marker! It took me too long to figure that out ...)

title: The Lion King
description: The Lion King represents one of the rare times that a movie-to-game conversion actually worked and granted us a pretty good game. (Gamefan magazine actually voted this game "Movie to Game Translation of the Year 1994".) Based on the Disney movie of the same name, you play as Simba, growing up to avenge his father's death. This is a platforming game where you start out as playing Simba as a young cub, and later control him as an adult. (Only the first level is playable in this demo version.) The graphics and sounds are great, as you would expect from a Disney-based property. The controls are responsive as well. Try it out if you're a fan of the movie and/or platforming games in general!

title: The Search for Freedom
description: Clearly a lot of work has gone into The Search for Freedom. The author has intended it to incorporate the best of his favorite CRPGs, such as Pool of Radiance and Bard's Tale. The game takes place primarily from a first-person perspective as you explore the town and catacombs. Navigating the town is super confusing, since all of the walls and doors look exactly the same, so it's very difficult to know where you're going. There are plenty of locations to visit however and many NPCs to interact with. There is also an involved character creation and party system, as well as a long backing storyline which informs your adventures. Be sure to check out the extensive manual for much more detailed information about how everything works, especially since the keyboard-based controls can be difficult to get used to.

title: The Settlers
description: The Settlers is a long-running series of RTS (real-time strategy) games, of which this is the first. Well the Amiga was first, then the DOS version. (In some areas it was called "Serf City: Life is Feudal".) This game was included in the book 1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die, and the series continues to this day. Anywho, I honestly don't know much about RTS games so I will assume that if you enjoy other games in this genre (such as Warcraft and similar games) then you'll probably like this one, especially given its glowing reviews. Note that since this is only a demo you won't get the full experience of the "real" game.

title: The Terminator: Future Shock
description: Terminator: Future Shock was a game that probably never got the attention it deserved when it was released. As showcased in this playable demo version of the full version game, this game differs from Quake in that it offers a bit more in the way of plot, and a little less in the way of slick gameplay. The game engine can be a bit buggy at times, but this can be overlooked because of the (at the time) excellent graphics, sound effects, and the coolness factor of playing a game based on the Terminator movies. You also get to drive vehicles on some levels of the full game.

title: Theme Hospital
description: Theme Hospital (1997) is the second in the "Theme ..." series of games following Theme Park in 1994. As you might expect, in this game you are given the task of running a hospital, including both the physical building layout, hiring staff, and providing for hospital guests. There are a number of different fictional diseases that need to be treated, and specialized rooms and equipment that can eventually be purchased for that purpose. The game's graphics and sounds are great, as to be expected in a Bullfrog Productions game. This demo version provides a tutorial as you get a taste of what the full game offers.

title: Theme Park
description: Theme Park is a classic strategy game, and one of the earliest "tycoon"-style games. In this demo version, your ride selection is limited to just one ride type, and there are many other limits as well. However it does give you a sample of the full game: Good graphics (for its time!) and decent sound/music too. The game is a little unbalanced at times, but anyone who's played this will definitely remember it, as it has a unique look and feel! (The "Boooo! Boooo!" sound effect is what I mostly remember ...)

title: Tom & Jerry
description: Based on the popular cat and mouse cartoon characters, Tom and Jerry is a fun sidescrolling game. It is similar to what you might find on the Nintendo NES or Super Nintendo systems. The object is to hop through the levels, throwing balls at enemies to eliminate them and get to the exits. Well made EGA graphics and decent sound effects as well as pretty tight controls will make this a fun yet challenging game for fans of sidescrolling, jumping platform action. (The original developer released this game for free on their website.)

title: Tomb Raider
description: The game that made Lara Croft a virtual star, and launched the entire series of Tomb Raider games. The game may seem somewhat bland by today's standards but it was quite popular upon its release, and NOT just because of certain attributes of its star character. One of the first of many 3rd-person 3D shooters. (Note: Press F1 in the game to toggle high resolution mode for better graphics.)

title: Tubes
description: Tubes is an interesting combination of several falling block style games, most notably KLAX. Here your goal, as in KLAX, is to create lines of atoms. As the variously colored atoms stream through the various tubes (hence the name) you can store up several at a time, or drop them immediately into the beaker (playing field). Overall a decent version of the game, although presenting it in a new way, it adds little in the way of features.

title: Tyrian
description: Tyrian is a shooting game that is somewhat similar to the Apogee offering "Raptor: Call of the Shadows". The object is, as so often the case for this particular genre, to blow everything up! It's a detailed and graphically intense space shoot-em-up with advanced (for the time) graphical effects and great sound/music. It also features an interesting plotline (for a shooting game) and many secret levels/bonuses to find. (Tyrian has been released as freeware by Jason Emery. You can download the full version of Tyrian 2000 for free at GOG.com.)

title: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
description: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar is, unsurprisingly, the fourth in the famous and influential Ultima series of fantasy RPGs. In 1996 Computer Gaming World placed Ultima IV #2 on its "Best PC Games of All Time", and for good reason. Ultima 4 is considered a big step forward for the series, and for computer role-playing games in general. The world of Britannia is fleshed out more than the first three games and there is a lot more story and personality evident in the game and the world itself. Although the graphics are crude by today's standards, it's the gameplay of story, exploration, battles (using a great environmentally-aware battle system) and character customization that make the game a true classic. Worth playing for RPG fans, but take note that since it was made in 1987 this is a true hardcore old-school RPG with no hand holding that will take considerable effort to learn and get into! (Note that the full version of the game along with full manuals and other extras is available via GOG.com; free registration is required to download and play it.)

title: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss
description: Ultima Underworld was a revolutionary game when it was released, introducing new features to the RPG genre including real-time 3D graphics which even in some ways surpassed Doom (released the next year in 1993).
